sentences.zh: 慕容儁

translations.literal: Murong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun

sentences.zh: 慕容儁，字宣英，皝之第二子也。

translations.literal: Murong Jun, courtesy name Xuanying, was the second son of Murong Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun, styled Xuanying, was Murong Huang's second son.

sentences.zh: 初，廆常言：「吾積福累仁，子孫當有中原。

translations.literal: At first, Gui often said, "I have accumulated blessings and piled up benevolence; my descendants shall obtain the Central Plains."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Murong Gui was fond of saying, "I have built up merit through kindness; my descendants are meant to hold the Central Plains."

sentences.zh: 」既而生俊，廆曰：「此兒骨相不恆，吾家得之矣。

translations.literal: " Afterwards Jun was born, and Gui said, "This child's bones and appearance are not ordinary; our house has obtained it."
translations.idiomatic: " After Murong Jun was born, he said, "This boy's bearing is out of the ordinary; our line has finally gained the heir it needs."

sentences.zh: 」及長，身長八尺二寸，姿貌魁偉，博觀圖書，有文武幹略。

translations.literal: " When he had grown up, he was eight chi two cun in height, his bearing was grand and imposing, he broadly examined maps and books, and he possessed civil and martial capacity and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, he stood eight feet two inches tall, carried himself with towering strength, read widely in the classics and histories, and showed both literary judgment and military resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 皝為燕王，拜俊假節、安北將軍、東夷校尉、左賢王、燕王世子。

translations.literal: When Huang was Prince of Yan, he appointed Jun provisional staff of authority, General Who Pacifies the North, Colonel of the Eastern Yi, Worthy King of the Left, and heir apparent of the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Huang became Prince of Yan, he invested Murong Jun with acting credentials of rank, the title General Who Pacifies the North, the post of Colonel of the Eastern Barbarians, the title Worthy King of the Left, and succession as heir to the Yan princedom.

sentences.zh: 皝死，，僭即燕王位，依春秋列國故事稱元年，赦於境內。

translations.literal: When Huang died, [Jun] usurpedly assumed the position of Prince of Yan, according to the Spring and Autumn Annals' precedent of the feudal states called it year one, and proclaimed amnesty within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Huang died, Murong Jun took the Yan throne without Jin's mandate, opened his reign with a "first year" after the custom of the Spring and Autumn hegemons, and declared an amnesty throughout his domain.

sentences.zh: 是時石季龍死，趙、魏大亂，俊將圖兼併之計，以慕容恪為輔國將軍，慕容評為輔弼將軍，陽騖為輔義將軍，慕容垂為前鋒都督、建鋒將軍，簡精卒二十餘萬以待期。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Jilong died, Zhao and Wei were in great chaos, and Jun planned a scheme of annexation, appointing Murong Ke as Assistant State General, Murong Ping as Assistant Support General, Yang Wu as Assistant Righteousness General, Murong Chui as area commander-in-chief of the van and General Who Establishes the Point, and selecting more than two hundred thousand picked soldiers to await the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu had just died, throwing Zhao and Wei into turmoil; Murong Jun set his mind on annexation, named Murong Ke general of state support, Murong Ping general of the princely establishment, Yang Wu general of righteous support, and Murong Chui van commander and "edge-setting" general, and readied more than two hundred thousand picked troops for the hour of decision.

sentences.zh: 是歲，穆帝使謁者陳沈拜俊為使持節、侍中、大都督、都督河北諸軍事、幽、冀、並、平四州牧、大將軍、大單于、燕王，承制封拜一如廆、皝故事。

translations.literal: That year, Emperor Mu dispatched Herald Chen Shen to invest Jun as bearer of staff and credentials, attendant-in-ordinary, grand area commander, area commander-in-chief of all military affairs north of the He, shepherd of the four provinces You, Ji, Bing, and Ping, grand general, great shanyu, and Prince of Yan, with authority to enfeoff and appoint on his own as in the precedents of Gui and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: The same year Emperor Mu sent the herald Chen Shen to appoint Murong Jun bearer of the imperial staff, palace attendant, supreme commander with authority over all Hebei forces, governor of You, Ji, Bing, and Ping, grand general, great chanyu, and Prince of Yan, empowering him to issue titles and appointments on his own authority, exactly as Murong Gui and Murong Huang had done.

sentences.zh: 明年，俊率三軍南伐，出自盧龍，次於無終。

translations.literal: The next year, Jun led the three armies on a southern campaign, issued from Lulong, and halted at Wuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Murong Jun marched south at the head of three armies, debouched through Lulong, and encamped at Wuzhong.

sentences.zh: 石季龍幽州刺史王午棄城走，留其將王他守薊。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong's inspector of You, Wang Wu, abandoned the city and fled, leaving his general Wang Ta to hold Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's governor of You, Wang Wu, abandoned his post and fled, leaving his officer Wang Ta to defend Ji.

sentences.zh: 俊攻陷其城，斬他，因而都之。

translations.literal: Jun attacked and took the city, beheaded Ta, and thereupon made it his capital.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun stormed the city, executed Wang Ta, and transferred his capital there.

sentences.zh: 徙廣甯、上谷人于徐無，代郡人於凡城而還。

translations.literal: He moved the people of Guangning and Shanggu to Xu Wu, the people of Dai commandery to Fancheng, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled the people of Guangning and Shanggu at Xuwu, shifted the population of Dai commandery to Fancheng, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及冉閔殺石祗，僭稱大號，遣其使人常煒聘於俊。

translations.literal: When Ran Min killed Shi Zhi and usurped the grand title, he sent his envoy Chang Wei to pay a court visit to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: After Ran Min murdered Shi Zhi and proclaimed himself emperor, he dispatched his envoy Chang Wei to treat with Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 俊引之觀下，使其記室封裕詰之曰：「冉閔養息常才，負恩篡逆，有何祥應而僭稱大號？

translations.literal: Jun led him below the hall and had his secretary Feng Yu question him, saying, "Ran Min was raised with common talent, betrayed grace and usurped in rebellion—what auspicious response does he have that he dares usurp the grand title?
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun had him brought beneath the dais and told his secretary Feng Yu to press him: "Ran Min is a man of middling parts raised from nowhere; he has turned on his benefactors and seized the throne—what portent could justify such a usurpation?

sentences.zh: 」煒曰：「天之所興，其致不同，狼烏紀于三王，麟龍表于漢、魏。

translations.literal: " Wei said, "What Heaven raises differs in its manifestations; the wolf and crow were recorded under the Three Kings, the unicorn and dragon appeared in Han and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang Wei replied, "Heaven's chosen show different signs: wolves and crows were chronicled under the Three Dynasties, qilin and dragons appeared in Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 寡君應天馭曆，能無祥乎！

translations.literal: Our lord answers to Heaven and controls the calendar—can there be no auspicious signs!
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign answers to Heaven and holds the calendar—how could omens be wanting?

sentences.zh: 且用兵殺伐，哲王盛典，湯、武親行誅放，而仲尼美之。

translations.literal: Moreover using arms and killing is the sage-kings' great canonical rite; Tang and Wu personally carried out executions and banishments, and Confucius praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover raising armies and striking down enemies were the great rites of the sage-kings: Tang and Wu themselves marched to punish and banish the wicked, and Confucius praised their deed.

sentences.zh: 魏武養于宦官，莫知所出，眾不盈旅，遂能終成大功。

translations.literal: Wei Wu was raised among eunuchs and none knew his origins; his host did not fill a brigade, yet he was able finally to accomplish a great merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei overlord grew up in a eunuch's household; no one knew his bloodline, and his following scarcely filled a company—yet he founded an empire.

sentences.zh: 暴胡酷亂，蒼生屠膾，寡君奮劍而誅除之，黎元獲濟，可謂功格皇天，勳侔高祖。

translations.literal: The violent Hu were cruelly chaotic; the black-haired people were butchered like minced meat; our lord brandished his sword and executed them; the black-haired people obtained relief—it may be called merit matching August Heaven, merit equal to the High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: While the barbarian hordes ran wild and common folk were slaughtered like meat on the block, our prince took up the sword and swept them away, giving the people respite—his achievement reaches to high Heaven and rivals Gaozu's own.

sentences.zh: 恭承乾命，有何不可？

translations.literal: Reverently inheriting the Qian mandate—what is impermissible?
translations.idiomatic: Having reverently received Heaven's charge, what is wrong with that?

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「石祗去歲使張舉請救，雲璽在襄國，其言信不？

translations.literal: " Yu said, "Shi Zhi last year sent Zhang Ju to request aid, saying the seal was at Xiangguo—is his word trustworthy?
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Yu said, "When Shi Zhi last year sent Zhang Ju pleading for rescue, he claimed the Heirloom Seal was at Xiangguo—was that true?

sentences.zh: 又聞閔鑄金為己象，壞而不成，奈何言有天命？

translations.literal: I have also heard Min cast a gold image of himself and it broke and did not succeed—how then speak of a Heaven mandate?
translations.idiomatic: We also hear Ran Min cast a golden likeness of himself only to see it crumble unfinished—how can you invoke a mandate from Heaven?

sentences.zh: 」煒曰：「誅胡之日，在鄴者略無所遺，璽何從而向襄國，此求救之辭耳。

translations.literal: " Wei said, "On the day the Hu were executed, those in Ye were nearly none left over—how could the seal have gone toward Xiangguo? This is language of begging for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang Wei said, "The day the barbarians were massacred in Ye, scarcely anyone survived; how could the seal have slipped away to Xiangguo? That tale was spun to beg for help.

sentences.zh: 天之神璽，實在寡君。

translations.literal: Heaven's divine seal is truly with our lord.
translations.idiomatic: The true divine tally rests with our sovereign.

sentences.zh: 且妖孽之徒，欲假奇眩眾，或改作萬端，以神其事。

translations.literal: Moreover the ilk of prodigies and portents desire by strange means to dazzle the multitude, or alter and make myriad changes to spiritify their affair.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, charlatans who trade on omens will invent marvels to dazzle the mob and dress their cause in wonders.

sentences.zh: 寡君今已握乾府，類上帝，四海懸諸掌，大業集于身，何所求慮而取信此乎！

translations.literal: Our lord now holds the treasury of Qian, performs the sacrifice to High God; the four seas hang in his palm; the great enterprise gathers on his person—what seeking and worry that he should take credence in this!
translations.idiomatic: Our prince already holds the celestial register, sacrifices to the Supreme Lord, has the realm cupped in his hand, and bears the full weight of the enterprise—why should he need such gossip to prove anything?

sentences.zh: 鑄形之事，所未聞也。

translations.literal: As for the matter of casting a form, I have not heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: As for casting a golden image, I have heard nothing of the sort.

sentences.zh: 」俊既銳信舉言，又欣于閔鑄形之不成也，必欲審之，乃積薪置火於其側，命裕等以意喻之。

translations.literal: Since Jun keenly believed Ju's words, and was pleased that Min's casting form did not succeed, he was determined to verify it, so he piled firewood and set fire beside him, ordering Yu and the others to hint at their intention to him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun, eager to credit Zhang Ju's story and gratified that Ran Min's casting had failed, resolved to test Chang Wei: he stacked firewood and lit a blaze at his side and told Feng Yu and the rest to make their meaning plain.

sentences.zh: 煒神色自若，抗言曰：「結髮已來，尚不欺庸人，況千乘乎！

translations.literal: Wei's expression was calm and self-possessed; he declared, "Since tying the hair I have not deceived even a common man, how much less a state with a thousand chariots!
translations.idiomatic: Chang Wei remained perfectly composed and declared, "Since I came of age I have never lied to a commoner—would I lie to the lord of a thousand chariots?

sentences.zh: 巧詐虛言以救死者，使臣所不為也。

translations.literal: Cunning fraud and empty words to save the dying—that which your servant does not do.
translations.idiomatic: I will not save my skin with clever lies.

sentences.zh: 直道受戮，死自分耳。

translations.literal: I receive execution on the straight path; death is my allotted share.
translations.idiomatic: Give me the honest death of an envoy; I accept my fate.

sentences.zh: 益薪速火，君之大惠。

translations.literal: Add fuel and hasten the fire—that is your great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Pile on the wood and fan the flames—that would be a kindness.

sentences.zh: 」左右勸俊殺之，俊曰：「古者兵交，使在其間，此亦人臣常事。

translations.literal: " Those at left and right urged Jun to kill him; Jun said, "Of old when armies crossed, envoys were between them—this too is a servitor's constant affair.
translations.idiomatic: " Attendants urged Murong Jun to kill him, but Jun said, "When ancient hosts met, envoys still passed between them—such hazard is an envoy's common lot.

sentences.zh: 」遂赦之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " So he spared him.

sentences.zh: 遣慕容恪略地中山，慕容評攻王午于魯口。

translations.literal: He sent Murong Ke to seize territory in Zhongshan, Murong Ping to attack Wang Wu at Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Murong Ke to overrun Zhongshan and Murong Ping to strike Wang Wu at Lukou.

sentences.zh: 恪次唐城，冉閔將白同、中山太守侯龕固守不下。

translations.literal: Ke halted at Tangcheng; Ran Min's generals Bai Tong and Zhongshan governor Hou Kan firmly defended and did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke halted at Tangcheng, where Ran Min's officers Bai Tong and the defender of Zhongshan, Hou Kan, held the walls and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 恪留其將慕容彪攻之，進討常山。

translations.literal: Ke left his general Murong Biao to assault them and advanced to punish Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke left Murong Biao to press the siege and marched to pacify Changshan.

sentences.zh: 評次南安，王午遣其將鄭生距評。

translations.literal: Ping halted at Nan'an; Wang Wu sent his general Zheng Sheng to oppose Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping encamped at Nan'an; Wang Wu sent Zheng Sheng to block him.

sentences.zh: 評逆擊，斬之，侯龕逾城出降。

translations.literal: Ping met and struck him, beheaded him; Hou Kan crossed over the wall and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping intercepted and killed Zheng Sheng; Hou Kan then came down from the walls and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 恪進克中山，斬白同。

translations.literal: Ke advanced and took Zhongshan, beheaded Bai Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke pressed on, took Zhongshan, and executed Bai Tong.

sentences.zh: 俊軍令嚴明，諸將無所犯。

translations.literal: Jun's army commands were strict and clear; the various generals had nothing they violated.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun's military law was strict, and none of his generals molested the people.

sentences.zh: 閔章武太守賈堅率郡兵邀評戰于高城，擒堅於陣，斬首三千餘級。

translations.literal: Min's Zhangwu governor Jia Jian led commandery soldiers to intercept Ping in battle at Gaocheng; [Ping] captured Jian in the ranks and beheaded more than three thousand levels.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min's governor of Zhangwu, Jia Jian, led county militia against Murong Ping at Gaocheng; Ping captured Jia Jian on the field and took more than three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 是歲丁零翟鼠及冉閔將劉准等率其所部降于俊，封鼠歸義王，拜准左司馬。

translations.literal: That year the Dingling chief Zhai Shu and Ran Min's general Liu Zhun and others led their departments to surrender to Jun; [Jun] enfeoffed Shu as Prince of Submitting Righteousness and appointed Zhun as left major of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The same year Dingling leader Zhai Shu and Ran Min's officer Liu Zhun brought their commands over to Murong Jun, who enfeoffed Zhai Shu as prince of "returning allegiance" and named Liu Zhun left marshal of the army.

sentences.zh: 時鮮卑段勤初附於俊，其後復叛。

translations.literal: At that time Xianbei Duan Qin first attached to Jun, afterward rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei chief Duan Qin had lately submitted to Murong Jun but rose again in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 俊遣慕容恪及相國封弈討冉閔于安喜，慕容垂討段勤於繹幕，俊如中山，為二軍聲勢。

translations.literal: Jun sent Murong Ke and Chancellor of State Feng Yi to punish Ran Min at Anxi, Murong Chui to punish Duan Qin at Yimù, and Jun went to Zhongshan to lend momentum to the two armies.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun dispatched Murong Ke and Chancellor Feng Yi against Ran Min at Anxi, Murong Chui against Duan Qin at Yimu, and himself rode to Zhongshan to stiffen both wings.

sentences.zh: 閔懼，奔於常山，恪追及于泒水。

translations.literal: Min feared and fled to Changshan; Ke overtook him at the Gu River.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min broke and fled for Changshan; Murong Ke overtook him on the Gu River.

sentences.zh: 閔威名素振，眾咸憚之。

translations.literal: Min's awesome name had always shaken [them]; the host all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min's terrible reputation preceded him, and every soldier dreaded him.

sentences.zh: 恪謂諸將曰：「閔師老卒疲，實為難用；

translations.literal: Ke said to the various generals, "Min's army is old and the soldiers weary—they are truly hard to use;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke told his officers, "Ran Min's men are worn from long campaigning—they are a brittle instrument.

sentences.zh: 加其勇而無謀，一夫之敵耳。

translations.literal: added he is brave but without stratagem—an enemy for a single man only.
translations.idiomatic: He trusts raw courage and has no plan—he is no more than a champion brawler.

sentences.zh: 雖有甲兵，不足擊也。

translations.literal: Although he has armored troops, they are not enough to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever armored host he brings, we need not fear a straight clash.

sentences.zh: 吾今分軍為三部，掎角以待之。

translations.literal: I now divide the army into three parts, to hook-horn and await him.
translations.idiomatic: I will split our army into three wings and wait in pincer formation.

sentences.zh: 閔性輕銳，又知吾軍勢非其敵，必出萬死沖吾中軍。

translations.literal: Min's nature is light and keen, and again knowing our army's momentum is not his enemy, he will assuredly issue from ten thousand deaths and charge our center army.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min is rash; knowing he cannot match our strength, he will stake everything on smashing our center.

sentences.zh: 吾今貫甲厚陣以俟其至，諸君但厲卒，從旁須其戰合，夾而擊之，蔑不克也。

translations.literal: I now string armor in a thick formation to await his arrival; you gentlemen only sharpen the soldiers, from the side wait until battle is joined, strike from both sides—none will not be overcome.
translations.idiomatic: I shall form a deep, heavy shield line to receive him. You need only ready your men, watch for the clash, then close from both flanks—he cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 」及戰，敗之，斬首七千餘級，擒閔，送之，斬于龍城。

translations.literal: When battle joined, they defeated him, beheaded more than seven thousand levels, captured Min, sent him, and beheaded him at Dragon City.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, they broke him, took more than seven thousand heads, seized Ran Min, conveyed him north, and executed him at Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 恪屯軍呼沲。

translations.literal: Ke encamped the army at Hutuo.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke encamped on the Hutuo.

sentences.zh: 閔將蘇亥遣其將金光率騎數千襲恪，恪逆擊，斬之，亥大懼，奔於并州。

translations.literal: Min's general Su Hai sent his general Jin Guang leading several thousand cavalry to raid Ke; Ke met and struck him, beheaded him; Hai greatly feared and fled to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min's officer Su Hai sent Jin Guang with thousands of horse to fall on Murong Ke; Murong Ke turned, cut Jin Guang down, and Su Hai fled in terror to Bing province.

sentences.zh: 恪進據常山，段勤懼而請降，遂進攻鄴。

translations.literal: Ke advanced and occupied Changshan; Duan Qin feared and requested surrender, whereupon he advanced to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke pushed into Changshan; Duan Qin begged to capitulate, and Ke then drove on Ye.

sentences.zh: 閔將蔣幹閉城距守。

translations.literal: Min's general Jiang Gan closed the city and defended against siege.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min's general Jiang Gan barred the gates of Ye.

sentences.zh: 俊又遣慕容評等率騎一萬會攻鄴。

translations.literal: Jun again dispatched Murong Ping and others to lead ten thousand cavalry to join the assault on Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun again sent Murong Ping with ten thousand horsemen to join the siege of Ye.

sentences.zh: 是時䴏巢于俊正陽殿之西椒，生三雛，項上有豎毛；

translations.literal: At that time fish-hawks nested on the western pepper-tree of Jun's Zhengyang Hall, bearing three chicks; on their necks were vertical feathers;
translations.idiomatic: That season ospreys nested on the pepper tree west of Murong Jun's Zhengyang Hall and hatched three chicks, each bearing an upright crest on its neck;

sentences.zh: 凡城獻異鳥，五色成章。

translations.literal: Fancheng presented a strange bird, five-colored and patterned.
translations.idiomatic: Fancheng offered up a polychrome bird of extraordinary plumage.

sentences.zh: 俊謂群僚曰：「是何祥也？

translations.literal: Jun said to the host of officials, "What omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun asked his court, "What do these signs mean?

sentences.zh: 」咸稱：「䴏者，燕鳥也。

translations.literal: " They all said, "The 䴏 is the swallow family bird.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "The bird called 䴏 is Yan's fowl.

sentences.zh: 首有毛冠者，言大燕龍興，冠通天章甫之象也。

translations.literal: Those whose heads have feathered caps speak of the great Yan dragon rising; it is the image of caps through heaven and Zhangfu.
translations.idiomatic: The crested head means Great Yan's dragon is stirring—an emblem of the cap that unites All under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 巢正陽西椒者，言至尊臨軒朝萬國之征也。

translations.literal: Nesting on the western pepper-tree of Zhengyang speaks of the sign of the august supreme facing south and holding court over the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: A nest on the west-facing pepper tree of Zhengyang Hall foretells the Son of Heaven holding court over the myriad kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 三子者，數應三統之驗也。

translations.literal: The three chicks are the verification corresponding to the three systems' number.
translations.idiomatic: Three fledglings answer to the numerology of the Three Systems.

sentences.zh: 神鳥五色，言聖朝將繼五行之籙以禦四海者也。

translations.literal: The divine bird's five colors speak of the sage court about to inherit the five phases' tally to rule the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: The five-hued numinous fowl means this sacred court will take up the succession of the Five Powers and command the four seas.

sentences.zh: 」俊覽之大悅。

translations.literal: Jun examined it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun heard them out with deep satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 既而蔣幹率銳卒五千出城挑戰，慕容評等擊敗之，斬首四千餘級，幹單騎還鄴。

translations.literal: Afterward Jiang Gan led five thousand crack soldiers out of the city to challenge; Murong Ping and the others defeated them, beheaded more than four thousand levels, and Gan alone on horseback returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiang Gan sallied with five thousand picked troops; Murong Ping threw him back, claimed more than four thousand heads, and Jiang Gan galloped back alone into Ye.

sentences.zh: 於是群臣勸俊稱尊號，俊答曰：「吾本幽漠射獵之鄉，被髮左衽之俗，歷數之籙寧有分邪！

translations.literal: Thereupon the host of officials urged Jun to claim the exalted title; Jun replied, "I am originally from the villages of Youmo where we shoot and hunt, the customs of disheveled hair and left lapping—can there be a portion in the succession's tally?
translations.idiomatic: Then the ministers pressed Murong Jun to take the imperial title. He answered, "My people spring from the northern wastes of bow and hunt, from loosened hair and left-lapped robes—what share could we have in Heaven's numbered mandate?

sentences.zh: 卿等苟相褒舉，以覬非望，實匪寡德所宜聞也。

translations.literal: You gentlemen hasten to praise and lift up, gazing toward what is not to be hoped—it is truly not what my meager virtue should hear."
translations.idiomatic: If you praise me beyond measure and reach for what is improper, you burden a man of slight virtue with what he dare not hear."

sentences.zh: 」慕容恪、封弈討王午于魯口，降之。

translations.literal: Murong Ke and Feng Yi punished Wang Wu at Lukou and made him submit.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke and Feng Yi campaigned against Wang Wu at Lukou and forced his surrender.

sentences.zh: 尋而慕容評攻克鄴城，送冉閔妻子僚屬及其文物于中山。

translations.literal: Shortly Murong Ping captured the city of Ye, sent Ran Min's wife, children, subordinates, and cultural relics to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Murong Ping took Ye and convoyed Ran Min's family, household, and regalia to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 先是，蔣幹以傳國璽送於建鄴，俊欲神其事業，言曆運在己，乃詐云閔妻得之以獻，賜號曰「奉璽君」，因以僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，建元曰元璽，署置百官。

translations.literal: Before this, Jiang Gan had sent the transmitted-state seal to Jianye; Jun desired to spiritify his enterprise, saying the calendar's luck was in himself, so he falsely said Min's wife obtained it and presented it—he granted her title "Lady Who Presented the Seal," whereupon he usurpedly assumed the position emperor of China, proclaimed a great amnesty within the borders, established the era name Yuanxi, and installed the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jiang Gan had forwarded the Heirloom Seal to the Jin court at Jiankang; Murong Jun, wanting to sacralize his own rule and claim the mandate had settled on him, pretended that Ran Min's wife had found it and offered it up. He ennobled her as "Consort Who Surrendered the Seal," then seized the imperial title, declared a general amnesty, adopted the reign title Yuanxi, and filled out the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 以封弈為太尉，慕容恪為侍中，陽騖為尚書令，皇甫真為尚書左僕射，張希為尚書右僕射，宋活為中書監，韓恆為中書令，其餘封授各有差。

translations.literal: He appointed Feng Yi as grand commandant, Murong Ke as palace attendant, Yang Wu as director of the secretariat, Huangfu Zhen as left supervisor of the masters of writing, Zhang Xi as right supervisor, Song Huo as superintendent of the palace secretariat, Han Heng as palace secretariat director; the rest received fiefs and appointments each according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: He named Feng Yi grand commandant, Murong Ke palace attendant, Yang Wu director of the Secretariat, Huangfu Zhen senior deputy director, Zhang Xi junior deputy, Song Huo prefect of the palace writers, Han Heng chief secretary, while the rest of the suite received graded promotions.

sentences.zh: 追尊廆為高祖武宣皇帝，皝為太祖文明皇帝。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored Gui as Gaozu Martial and Exalted Emperor, Huang as Taizu Civil and Enlightened Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he elevated Murong Gui to Emperor Wuxuan the Exalted Ancestor and Murong Huang to Emperor Wenming the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷遣使詣俊，俊謂使者曰：「汝還白汝天子，我承人之乏，為中國所推，已為帝矣。

translations.literal: At that time the court sent an envoy to Jun; Jun said to the envoy, "You return and tell your Son of Heaven—I have succeeded where others failed, have been pushed forward by those within China, and am already emperor."
translations.idiomatic: When Jin sent envoys, Murong Jun told them, "Go back and inform your emperor: I stepped into a fallen line, have been acclaimed by the Central States, and already call myself emperor."

sentences.zh: 」初，石季龍使人探策于華山，得玉版，文曰：「歲在申酉，不絕如線。

translations.literal: At first Shi Jilong had sent men to divine by stalks on Mount Hua and obtained a jade plaque with text saying, "In the years Shen and You, not cut off like a thread.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Shi Hu had sent men to cast lots on Mount Hua and turned up a jade tablet reading, "In the shen and you years survival hangs by a thread;

sentences.zh: 歲在壬子，真人乃見。

translations.literal: in the year Renzi the True Man will appear."
translations.idiomatic: in the renzi year the True Lord will appear."

sentences.zh: 」及此，燕人咸以為俊之應也。

translations.literal: When it reached this, Yan people all considered it Jun's verification.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan court took this as proof that Murong Jun fulfilled the prophecy.

sentences.zh: 改司州為中州，置司隸校尉官。

translations.literal: He changed Sizhou to Central Province and installed the office of metropolitan commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed Si province Zhongzhou and created a metropolitan intendant's post.

sentences.zh: 群下言：「大燕受命，上承光紀黑精之君，運曆傳屬，代金行之後，宜行夏之時，服周之冕，旗幟尚黑，牲牡尚玄。

translations.literal: The host below said, "Great Yan has received the mandate; above it inherits from the lord of light's era black essence, the luck of the calendar passes down; succeeding the metal phase's afterward, it should practice Xia's seasons, wear Zhou's caps, flags and banners honor black, sacrificial victims honor dark."
translations.idiomatic: His ministers argued, "Great Yan holds the Mandate: it succeeds the Black Essence ruler of the Light-Era and carries the calendar forward after the Jin (metal) line. It should use the Xia calendar, wear the Zhou crown, fly black banners, and offer dark-hued victims."

sentences.zh: 」俊從之。

translations.literal: Jun followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun accepted their advice.

sentences.zh: 其從行文武、諸籓使人及登號之日者，悉增位三級。

translations.literal: Those who accompanied him in civil and military capacity, envoys of the various feudatories, and those present on the day of assuming the title—all received promotion of three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military followers, envoys from tributary domains, and everyone present on accession day rose three grades in rank.

sentences.zh: 泒河之師，守鄴之軍，下及戰士，賜各有差。

translations.literal: Those of the Gu River army, the army defending Ye, down to the common soldiers—gifts each according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: Troops who had fought on the Gu, the garrison of Ye, down to line soldiers—each received bounty by station.

sentences.zh: 臨陣戰亡者，將士加贈二等，士卒復其子孫。

translations.literal: Those who died in battle at the front: for generals and officers increased posthumous gifts two grades; for soldiers, exemption for their sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: The fallen on campaign received two extra steps of posthumous honor for officers; common soldiers' sons and grandsons were granted remit of service.

sentences.zh: 殿中舊人皆隨才擢敘。

translations.literal: The old personnel of the palace hall all followed talent in being promoted and ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Every veteran of the inner palace was reassigned by merit.

sentences.zh: 立其妻可足渾氏為皇后，世子曄為皇太子。

translations.literal: He established his wife Lady Kezhunhun as empress, heir apparent Ye as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated his consort of the Kezhunhun clan to empress and named his heir apparent Murong Ye crown prince.

sentences.zh: 晉甯朔將軍榮胡以彭城、魯郡叛降於俊。

translations.literal: Jin's General Who Extends the North Rong Hu with Pengcheng and Lu commandery rebel-surrendered to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's General Who Extends the North, Rong Hu, brought Pengcheng and Lu commandery over to Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 常山人李犢聚眾數千，反於普壁壘，俊遣慕容恪率眾討降之。

translations.literal: A man of Changshan, Li Du, gathered a host of several thousand and rebelled at Pubi rampart; Jun dispatched Murong Ke leading a host to punish and subdue him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Du of Changshan raised several thousand men at Pubi fortress; Murong Jun sent Murong Ke, who crushed the rising and accepted their surrender.

sentences.zh: 初，冉閔既敗，王午自號安國王。

translations.literal: At first, after Ran Min was defeated, Wang Wu styled himself king of An state.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ran Min fell, Wang Wu had proclaimed himself king of An.

sentences.zh: 午既死，呂護復襲其號，保于魯口。

translations.literal: After Wu died, Lu Hu again seized his title and held out at Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Wu died, Lü Hu copied his title and entrenched himself at Lukou.

sentences.zh: 恪進討走之，遣前軍悅綰追及于野王，悉降其眾。

translations.literal: Ke advanced to punish and drove him off, dispatched vanguard Yue Wan to overtake him at Yewang, and wholly submitted his host.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke advanced, broke his line, sent his van leader Yue Wan in pursuit to Yewang, and compelled the whole force to capitulate.

sentences.zh: 姚襄以梁國降於俊。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang with Liang state surrendered to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang brought the Liang principality over to Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 以慕容評為都督秦、雍、益、梁、江、揚、荊、徐、袞、豫十州河南諸軍事，權鎮于洛水；

translations.literal: He appointed Murong Ping as area commander-in-chief of Qin, Yong, Yi, Liang, Jiang, Yang, Jing, Xu, Yan, Yu all military affairs south of the Yellow River's ten provinces, with temporary garrison on the Luo River;
translations.idiomatic: He named Murong Ping commander of Qin, Yong, Yi, Liang, Jiang, Yang, Jing, Xu, Yan, and Yu—every command south of the Yellow River—and bivouacked him on the Luo.

sentences.zh: 慕容彊為前鋒都督、都督荊、徐二州緣淮諸軍事，進據河南。

translations.literal: Murong Qiang served as area commander-in-chief of the van and area commander-in-chief of military affairs along the Huai for Jing and Xu provinces, advanced, and occupied Henan south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He named Murong Qiang van-area commander with authority along the Huai over Jing and Xu, and Murong Qiang advanced to seize the south bank of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 俊自和龍至薊城，幽冀之人為東遷，互相驚擾，所在屯結。

translations.literal: Jun from Helong to Jicheng; the people of You and Ji for eastward relocation mutually alarmed and harassed each other, everywhere encamping and banding together.
translations.idiomatic: As Murong Jun traveled from Helong to Ji, the populace of You and Ji, fearing forced migration eastward, panicked, scattered, and rallied everywhere in armed bands.

sentences.zh: 其下請討之，俊曰：「群小以朕東巡，故相惑耳。

translations.literal: His subordinates requested to punish them; Jun said, "The petty host, because I am touring east, therefore mutually delude each other.
translations.idiomatic: His generals begged leave to strike them; Murong Jun said, "These folk only stir because they heard I was moving east.

sentences.zh: 今朕既至，尋當自定。

translations.literal: Now that I have arrived, presently they will settle themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am here, calm will return of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 然不虞之備亦不可不為。

translations.literal: Yet provision against the unexpected also cannot be left undone.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, precautions against the unforeseen had to be taken.

sentences.zh: 」於是令內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered inner and outer cordon alert.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered martial law throughout the capital and the hinterland.

sentences.zh: 苻生河內太守王會、黎陽太守韓高以郡歸俊。

translations.literal: Fu Sheng's Henei governor Wang Hui and Liyang governor Han Gao with their commanderies submitted to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng's governors of Henei and Liyang, Wang Hui and Han Gao, surrendered their districts to Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 晉蘭陵太守孫黑、濟北太守高柱、建興太守高甕各以郡叛歸於俊。

translations.literal: Jin's Lanling governor Sun Hei, Jibei governor Gao Zhu, and Jianxing governor Gao Weng each with their commanderies rebelled and submitted to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's prefects of Lanling, Jibei, and Jianxing—Sun Hei, Gao Zhu, and Gao Weng—each broke with the court and brought their commanderies over to Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 初，俊車騎大將軍、范陽公劉寧屯據蕕城，降於苻氏，至此，率戶二千詣薊歸罪，拜後將軍。

translations.literal: At first, Jun's chariot-and-horse grand general, Duke of Fanyang Liu Ning, had occupied Raocheng and submitted to the Fu clan; reaching this point, he led two thousand households to Ji to acknowledge guilt, and was appointed rear general.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun's chariot general and Duke of Fanyang, Liu Ning, had once held Raocheng for the Fu regime; now he brought two thousand households to Ji to submit and was named rear general.

sentences.zh: 高句麗王釗遣使謝恩，貢其方物。

translations.literal: The king of Gaogouli, Jian, dispatched envoys to thank for grace and present tribute of local products.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Goguryeo, Jian, sent envoys to express gratitude and offer local tribute.

sentences.zh: 俊以釗為營州諸軍事、征東大將軍、營州刺史，封樂浪公，王如故。

translations.literal: Jun appointed Jian as area commander-in-chief of Yingzhou, east-conquering grand general, and inspector of Yingzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Lelang, king as before.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun named Jian area commander for Yingzhou, grand general for the eastern expedition, and governor of Yingzhou, enfeoffed him as Duke of Lelang, and confirmed his royal title.

sentences.zh: 俊給事黃門侍郎申胤上言曰：

translations.literal: Jun's attendant at the yellow gate, Shen Yin, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yin, Murong Jun's gentleman attendant at the yellow gate, presented a memorial:

sentences.zh: 夫名尊禮重，先王之制。

translations.literal: As for name being exalted and ritual being weighty—the former kings' system.
translations.idiomatic: High titles and weighty ceremony were the institutions of the ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 冠冕之式，代或不同。

translations.literal: The forms of cap and crown—each age perhaps differed.
translations.idiomatic: The style of caps and crowns shifted from one age to the next.

sentences.zh: 漢以蕭、曹之功，有殊群辟，故劍履上殿，入朝不趨。

translations.literal: Han, because of Xiao and Cao's merit, had them differ from the host of nobles, therefore sword and shoes on the hall, entering court without hurrying.
translations.idiomatic: The Han honored Xiao He and Cao Cao above the peerage, granting them the right to wear sword and shoes in the audience hall and to enter court without the quickened step.

sentences.zh: 世無其功，則禮宜闕也。

translations.literal: When the age lacks such merit, then ritual properly is wanting.
translations.idiomatic: When no such merit exists, those privileges rightly fall away.

sentences.zh: 至於東宮，體此為儀，魏、晉因循，制不納舄。

translations.literal: As for the Eastern Palace, taking this as its model was the rite; Wei and Jin followed along, the system not admitting court slippers.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent's household modeled itself on that precedent; Wei and Jin continued the rule that court slippers were not worn in audience.

sentences.zh: 今皇儲過謙，准同百僚，禮卑逼下，有違朝式。

translations.literal: Now the imperial heir is overly modest, aligning with the hundred officials; ritual is low and presses down on inferiors, violating court form.
translations.idiomatic: Today the crown prince is excessively humble and ranks himself with ordinary ministers, which lowers ritual beneath its station and breaks court precedent.

sentences.zh: 太子有統天之重，而與諸王齊冠遠遊，非所以辨章貴賤也。

translations.literal: The crown prince bears the weight of ordering Heaven, yet with the various princes wears the same cap of distant roaming—it is not the means to distinguish exalted and base.
translations.idiomatic: The heir bears the charge of the cosmos yet shares the same "far-roaming" cap as the princes—this fails to mark rank between high and low.

sentences.zh: 祭饗朝慶，宜正服袞衣九文，冠冕九旒。

translations.literal: For sacrifices, feasts, and court congratulations, he should correct his dress to nine-patterned daimyo robe, cap with nine pendants.
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices, banquets, and court felicitations he should wear the nine-emblem sacral robe and the nine-tassel crown.

sentences.zh: 又仲冬長至，太陰數終，黃鐘產氣，綿微於下，此月閉關息旅，後不省方。

translations.literal: Moreover in mid-winter at the utmost of the yin, the Grand Yin's reckoning ends, the yellow bell produces qi, faintly continuing below; in this month gates are closed and hosts rested, afterward not inspecting the regions.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover at the winter solstice, when yin reaches its limit, the yellow-bell pitch stirs faintly below; that month is for closing the passes, resting the hosts, and suspending imperial tours of inspection.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》曰：「是月也，事欲靜，君子齊戒去聲色。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says, "In this month affairs desire stillness; the gentleman fasts and withdraws from sound and color.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says, "In that month affairs should be still; the gentleman fasts and puts aside music and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 」唯《周官》有天子之南郊從八能之說。

translations.literal: " Only the Rites of Zhou has the theory of the Son of Heaven's southern suburb following the eight powers.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Offices of Zhou describe the southern-suburb rite with the eight kinds of resonant performance.

sentences.zh: 或以有事至靈，非朝饗之節，故有樂作之理。

translations.literal: Some consider there being affairs reaching to the numinous, not the season of court feasting, therefore there is principle for music being performed.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that contact with the spirits is not the same as a court banquet, so music there has its justification.

sentences.zh: 王者慎微，禮從其重。

translations.literal: The king is cautious of the subtle; ritual follows the weighty.
translations.idiomatic: A true king is wary of small signs and lets ritual favor the stricter course.

sentences.zh: 前來二至闕鼓，不宜有設，今之鏗鏘，蓋以常儀。

translations.literal: Previously at the two solstices the drums were omitted—there should not have been setting; now the clanging, in general is because of constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the two solstices passed without the great drums; no such display should have been mounted—today's clamor is merely unthinking routine.

sentences.zh: 二至之禮、事殊餘節，猥動金聲，驚越神氣，施之宣養，實為未盡。

translations.literal: The two solstices' ritual, affairs differ from other seasons; vulgarly moving metal sound, startling and crossing the spirit qi, applying it to proclaiming nurture—truly is not yet exhaustive.
translations.idiomatic: The solstice observances differ from other festivals; to strike metal rashly, jar the spirits, and call that "nurturing" the realm falls short of what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 又朝服雖是古禮，絳褠始于秦、漢，迄於今代，遂相仍准。

translations.literal: Moreover court dress, although it is ancient ritual, the crimson lined robe began in Qin and Han; down to the present generation, thereupon mutually followed as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress is ancient in principle, but the crimson lined gown dates from Qin and Han and has since hardened into custom.

sentences.zh: 朔望正旦，乃具袞舄。

translations.literal: On new and full moon and new year's dawn, then they fully provide daimyo robe and court slippers.
translations.idiomatic: Only on the new and full moons and at New Year's did they don the full sacral robe with court shoes.

sentences.zh: 禮，諸侯旅見天子，不得終事者三，雨沾服失容，其在一焉。

translations.literal: Rite: when feudal lords travel to see the Son of Heaven, there are three cases of not being able to finish the affair—rain soaking the clothes and losing deportment is one among them.
translations.idiomatic: The canon says that when feudal lords audience the Son of Heaven, three things may cut the rite short—and rain that soaks the robes and spoils one's bearing is one.

sentences.zh: 今或朝日天雨，未有定儀。

translations.literal: Now sometimes on court audience day Heaven rains, and there is no fixed practice.
translations.idiomatic: Today, if rain falls on an audience day, there is no settled rule.

sentences.zh: 禮貴適時，不在過恭。

translations.literal: Rite esteems suiting the season; it does not lie in excessive deference.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual values timeliness, not exaggerated obeisance.

sentences.zh: 近以地濕不得納舄，而以袞襈改履。

translations.literal: Recently because the ground was wet they could not admit court slippers, and therefore with daimyo train changed to shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, because the ground was wet, court slippers were dispensed with and the sacral train was paired with ordinary shoes instead.

sentences.zh: 案言稱朝服，所以服之而朝，一體之間，上下二制，或廢或存，實乖禮意。

translations.literal: Investigating the wording saying court dress—therefore wearing it to court—within one body, upper and lower two systems, sometimes abolished sometimes existing—truly violates ritual intention.
translations.idiomatic: The text speaks of "court dress" for wearing in audience, yet the same body now follows two rules—sometimes shoes, sometimes not—which contradicts the meaning of the rite.

sentences.zh: 大燕受命，侔蹤虞、夏，諸所施行，宜損益定之，以為皇代永制。

translations.literal: Great Yan has received the mandate, tracks matching Yu and Xia; in what is implemented and carried out, it should be increased or decreased and fixed, to become the imperial age's perpetual system.
translations.idiomatic: Great Yan holds the Mandate and walks in the footsteps of Yu and Xia; its institutions should be weighed, adjusted, and fixed as the lasting code of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 俊曰：「其劍舄不趨，事下太常參議。

translations.literal: Jun said, "As for sword and slippers without hurrying—affair below the grand master of ceremonies for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun replied, "The matter of sword, shoes, and waived step—send it down to the chamberlain for rites for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 太子服袞冕，冠九旒，超級逼上，未可行也。

translations.literal: The crown prince wearing daimyo robe and crown, nine pendants, overstepping grade and pressing on superiors—not yet feasible.
translations.idiomatic: To dress the heir in the nine-tassel sacral crown would overleap rank and crowd his sovereign—this cannot be done yet.

sentences.zh: 冠服何容一施一廢，皆可詳定。」

translations.literal: How can cap and dress tolerate one applied and one abolished—all can be detailed and fixed."
translations.idiomatic: Cap and gown cannot be partly adopted and partly discarded; work out a single clear rule for each."

sentences.zh: 初，段蘭之子龕因冉閔之亂，擁眾東屯廣固，自號齊王，稱籓於建鄴，遣書抗中表之儀，非俊正位。

translations.literal: At first, Duan Lan's son Kan, taking advantage of Ran Min's turmoil, gathered a host and camped east at Guanggu, styled himself king of Qi, declared vassalage to Jianye, sent letters resisting the courtesy between cousins, not acknowledging Jun's orthodox position.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Duan Lan's son Kan had exploited Ran Min's chaos to rally men east at Guanggu, styled himself king of Qi, feigned submission to Jiankang, and in his letters rejected cousin-to-cousin etiquette, refusing to recognize Murong Jun's legitimacy.

sentences.zh: 俊遣慕容恪、慕容塵討之。

translations.literal: Jun dispatched Murong Ke and Murong Chen to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun sent Murong Ke and Murong Chen against him.

sentences.zh: 恪既濟河。

translations.literal: Ke had already crossed the He.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke crossed the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 龕弟羆驍勇有智計，言於龕曰：「慕容恪善用兵，加其眾旅既盛，恐不可抗也。

translations.literal: Duan Kan's younger brother Pi was fierce and brave and had stratagems; he spoke to Kan, saying, "Murong Ke is good at using troops, added to his host being already abundant—probably cannot be resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Kan's brother Pi was a fierce, clever fighter. He warned Kan, "Murong Ke is a master of war, and his army is huge—you are unlikely to withstand him.

sentences.zh: 若頓兵城下，雖復請降，懼終不聽。

translations.literal: If we halt troops below the city, although again requesting surrender, I fear in the end he will not listen.
translations.idiomatic: If we let him camp beneath the walls, even a later plea to surrender may not be heeded.

sentences.zh: 王但固守，羆請率精銳距之。

translations.literal: Your lordship only firmly defend; Pi requests to lead picked crack to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the city fast; let me lead picked troops to meet him in the field.

sentences.zh: 若其戰捷，王可馳來追擊，使虜匹馬無反。

translations.literal: If we win in battle, your lordship can gallop forth to pursue the attack, making the barbarians not a single horse return.
translations.idiomatic: If we win, you can ride out in pursuit and leave the enemy not a horse to carry home.

sentences.zh: 如其敗也，遽出請降，不失千戶侯也。

translations.literal: If it is like defeat, then quickly go out requesting surrender—not losing a thousand-household marquis.
translations.idiomatic: If we lose, you can still go out at once to sue for peace and keep at least a marquis's thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 」龕弗從。

translations.literal: " Kan did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Kan refused.

sentences.zh: 羆固請行，龕怒斬之，率眾三萬來距恪。

translations.literal: Pi firmly requested to go; Kan angrily beheaded him, led a host of thirty thousand to oppose Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Pi pressed his plan until Duan Kan, enraged, executed him, then marched thirty thousand men against Murong Ke.

sentences.zh: 恪遇龕于濟水之南，與戰，大敗之，遂斬其弟欽，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Ke encountered Kan south of the Ji River, battled with him, greatly defeated him, thereupon beheaded his younger brother Qin, wholly captured his host.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke met Duan Kan south of the Ji River, shattered his army, slew Kan's brother Qin, and took the entire force captive.

sentences.zh: 恪進圍廣固，諸將勸恪宜急攻之，恪曰：「軍勢有宜緩以克敵，有宜急而取之。

translations.literal: Ke advanced and besieged Guanggu; the various generals urged Ke should urgently attack him; Ke said, "Military momentum has cases where it is proper to be slow to overcome the enemy, cases where it is proper to be quick and take them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke closed on Guanggu. His officers urged a storm; he said, "Sometimes slow pressure wins; sometimes speed is right.

sentences.zh: 若彼我勢均，且有強援，慮腹背之患者，須急攻之，以速大利。

translations.literal: If enemy and we are evenly matched in strength, and moreover have strong aid, worrying about belly-and-back troubles—must urgently attack them, to speed great profit.
translations.idiomatic: When forces are even and strong relief threatens your rear, strike fast for decisive gain.

sentences.zh: 如其我強彼弱，外無寇援，力足制之者，當羈縻守之，以待其斃。

translations.literal: If it is like we are strong and they weak, outside without raider aid, strength sufficient to control them—should tether and guard them, to await their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: When you are strong, they weak, and no rescue threatens, hold them in a loose siege and wait for starvation to do its work.

sentences.zh: 兵法十圍五攻，此之謂也。

translations.literal: The art of war: ten encircle, five attack—this speaks of it.
translations.idiomatic: The canon says, 'Where you outnumber ten to one, surround; five to one, attack'—that is the point here.

sentences.zh: 龕恩結賊黨，眾未離心，濟南之戰，非不銳也，但其用之無術，以致敗耳。

translations.literal: Kan's grace has tied the bandit party; the host has not yet left its heart; at the battle of Jinan, it was not that they were not keen, but that in using them there was no art, thereby causing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Kan still commands the loyalty of his band; the army has not lost heart. They fought hard at Jinan but lacked a competent hand on the reins—that alone brought defeat.

sentences.zh: 今憑固天險，上下同心，攻守勢倍，軍之常法。

translations.literal: Now relying on the natural rampart, upper and lower share one heart, attack and defense double in force—this is the army's constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: He now holds heaven's sheer walls, his officers and men are of one mind, and offense and defense double his advantage—the textbook case in military science.

sentences.zh: 若其促攻，不過數旬，克之必矣，但恐傷吾士眾。

translations.literal: If we hasten attack, not passing several tens of days, taking it is certain; but I fear wounding our officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: A forced assault would crack the place in a matter of weeks, yet I shrink from wasting our men's lives.

sentences.zh: 自有事已來，卒不獲寧，吾每思之，不覺忘寢，亦何宜輕殘人命乎！

translations.literal: Since troubles began, the soldiers have not obtained peace; I each time think of it, without realizing forgetting sleep—how can it be proper lightly to mutilate human lives!
translations.idiomatic: Since the troubles began our troops have known no rest; whenever I think of it I forget sleep—how could I lightly throw away lives?

sentences.zh: 當持久以取耳。

translations.literal: We should be enduring to take them.
translations.idiomatic: We should wear them down over time and take them that way.

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆曰：「非所及也。

translations.literal: " The various generals all said, "This is not what we can match.
translations.idiomatic: His officers said, "None of us could have thought of that."

sentences.zh: 」乃築室反耕，嚴固圍壘。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they built houses and reversed plowing, strictly solidifying the encircling ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: So they settled in for a long siege, sent men out to farm, and threw up strong lines around the city.

sentences.zh: 龕所署徐州刺史王騰、索頭單于薛雲降於恪。

translations.literal: Kan's appointed inspector of Xuzhou Wang Teng and Wuhuan shanyu Xue Yun surrendered to Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Kan's governor of Xuzhou, Wang Teng, and the Wuhuan chanyu Xue Yun went over to Murong Ke.

sentences.zh: 段龕之被圍也，遣使詣建鄴請救。

translations.literal: When Duan Kan was besieged, he dispatched envoys to Jianye requesting rescue.
translations.idiomatic: While Duan Kan was under siege he sent to Jiankang begging for relief.

sentences.zh: 穆帝遣北中郎將荀羨赴之，憚虜強遷延不敢進。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu dispatched north center general Xun Xian to go to them; fearing the barbarians' strength, he delayed and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu sent the north-center general Xun Xian to their aid, but Xun Xian, dreading the enemy's strength, dragged his feet and would not march.

sentences.zh: 攻破陽都，斬王騰以歸。

translations.literal: He attacked and broke Yangdu, beheaded Wang Teng and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Yangdu instead, killed Wang Teng, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 恪遂克廣固，以龕為伏順將軍，徙鮮卑胡羯三千餘戶於薊，留慕容塵鎮廣固，恪振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Ke thereupon took Guanggu, appointed Kan as submissive-compliant general, moved more than three thousand households of Xianbei, Hu, and Jie to Ji, left Murong Chen to garrison Guanggu, and Ke returned with drums.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke then stormed Guanggu, named Duan Kan a general of forced allegiance, deported over three thousand Xianbei, Hu, and Jie households to Ji, left Murong Chen to hold the city, and marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 俊太子曄死，偽諡獻懷。

translations.literal: Jun's crown prince Ye died; he was given the posthumous title Xianhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun's crown prince Murong Ye died and received the posthumous name Xianhuai.

sentences.zh: ，復立次子暐為皇太子，赦其境內，改元曰光壽。

translations.literal: He again established the second son Wei (written 暐) as crown prince, proclaimed amnesty within the borders, changed the era name to Guangshou.
translations.idiomatic: He then named his second son Murong Wei crown prince, declared a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Guangshou.

sentences.zh: 遣其撫軍慕容垂、中軍慕容虔與護軍平熙等率步騎八萬討丁零敕勒於塞北，大破之，俘斬十餘萬級，獲馬十三萬匹，牛羊億余萬。

translations.literal: He dispatched his general Who Pacifies the Army Murong Chui, center army Murong Qian, with guard general Ping Xi and others leading infantry and cavalry eighty thousand to punish Dingling Chile north of the passes, greatly defeated them, captured and beheaded more than a hundred thousand levels, obtained horses one hundred thirty thousand head, cattle and sheep exceeding a hundred million.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Murong Chui, Murong Qian, Ping Xi, and others at the head of eighty thousand horse and foot against the Dingling and Tiele north of the frontier, shattered them, took over a hundred thousand heads and prisoners, seized a hundred thirty thousand horses, and countless cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 初，廆有駿馬曰赭白，有奇相逸力。

translations.literal: At first, Gui had a swift horse called Red-White, having strange appearance and extraordinary strength.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gui had once owned a famous charger named Red White, marked by an uncanny frame and exceptional stamina.

sentences.zh: 石季龍之伐棘城也，皝將出避難，欲乘之，馬悲鳴蹄齧，人莫能近。

translations.literal: When Shi Jilong campaigned against Jicheng, Huang was about to go out avoiding difficulty, wished to ride it; the horse mournfully neighed, hoof bit—none could approach.
translations.idiomatic: During Shi Hu's siege of Jicheng, Murong Huang tried to mount it to flee; the horse screamed and snapped at anyone who drew near.

sentences.zh: 皝曰：「此馬見異先朝，孤常仗之濟難，今不欲者，蓋先君之意乎！

translations.literal: Huang said, "This horse witnessed the unusual in the former court; I always relied on it to cross difficulty; now not desiring—probably is the former lord's intention!
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang said, "This beast bore me through the last crisis; now it refuses—perhaps that is my late father's will from beyond the grave.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: So he stayed.

sentences.zh: 季龍尋退，皝益奇之。

translations.literal: Jilong shortly withdrew; Huang increasingly thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu soon lifted the siege, and Murong Huang prized the horse all the more.

sentences.zh: 至是，四十九歲矣，而駿逸不虧，俊比之于鮑氏驄，命鑄銅以圖其象，親為銘贊，鐫勒其旁，置之薊城東掖門。

translations.literal: Reaching this point, forty-nine years had passed, yet swift gallop was not diminished; Jun compared it to Bao's dappled team, ordered casting bronze to picture its likeness, personally composed inscription and praise, carved on its side, placed east of Ji's east-side gate.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-nine years later it still ran like new; Murong Jun likened it to Bao Shuya's famous team, ordered a bronze statue cast in its image, inscribed his own eulogy on the flank, and set it up outside the east portal of Ji.

sentences.zh: 是歲，象成而馬死。

translations.literal: That year, the image was completed and the horse died.
translations.idiomatic: The year the statue was finished, the horse died.

sentences.zh: 匈奴單于賀賴頭率部落三萬五千降於俊，拜甯西將軍、雲中郡公，處之于代郡平舒城。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu shanyu Helaitou led tribes thirty-five thousand households to submit to Jun, appointed General Who Pacifies the West, Duke of Yunzhong commandery, settled them at Dai commandery Pingshu city.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu chanyu Helaitou brought thirty-five thousand households to submit; Murong Jun named him General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Yunzhong and settled them at Pingshu in Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉太山太守諸葛攸伐其東郡。

translations.literal: Jin's Taishan governor Zhuge You campaigned against his eastern commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's governor of Taishan, Zhuge You, attacked Murong Jun's eastern commandery.

sentences.zh: 俊遣慕容恪距戰，王師敗績。

translations.literal: Jun dispatched Murong Ke to oppose in battle; the royal army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun sent Murong Ke, who met the Jin host and broke it.

sentences.zh: 北中郎將謝萬先據梁、宋，懼而遁歸。

translations.literal: North center general Xie Wan first occupied Liang and Song, feared and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: The north-center general Xie Wan, who had held Liang and Song, panicked and ran.

sentences.zh: 恪進兵入寇河南，汝、潁、譙、沛皆陷，置守宰而還。

translations.literal: Ke advanced troops invading Henan, Ru, Ying, Qiao, Pei all fell, installed guards and shepherds and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke pushed into Henan, overran Ru, Ying, Qiao, and Pei, installed garrisons and magistrates, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俊自薊城遷於鄴，赦其境內，繕修宮殿，復銅雀台。

translations.literal: Jun moved from Jicheng to Ye, proclaimed amnesty within the borders, repaired the palace halls, restored the Bronze Bird Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun moved his capital from Ji to Ye, granted amnesty, restored the palace, and rebuilt the Bronze Bird Terrace.

sentences.zh: 廷尉監常煒上言：「大燕雖革命創制，至於朝廷銓謨，亦多因循魏、晉，唯祖父不殮葬者，獨不聽官身清朝，斯誠王教之首，不刊之式。

translations.literal: Court supervisor Chang Wei submitted a memorial saying, "Although Great Yan has by revolution created institutions, as for court selection and planning, it also largely follows along Wei and Jin; only for those whose grandfathers and fathers were not buried and encoffined, alone not permitting official body in the clear court—this is truly the head of kingly instruction, unalterable model.
translations.idiomatic: The court censor Chang Wei wrote, "Though Great Yan has founded a new order, its personnel policy still follows Wei and Jin—except for the rule that no one may hold office while his parents lie unburied, which is rightly the first principle of moral government and ought not to change lightly.

sentences.zh: 然禮貴適時，世或損益，是以高祖制三章之法，而秦人安之。

translations.literal: Yet ritual esteems suiting the season; the age perhaps increases or decreases; therefore the High Ancestor established the three-zhang law, and Qin people were at peace with it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rites must fit the times and may be tightened or loosened—Gaozu's three-article code calmed a shattered Qin.

sentences.zh: 自頃中州喪亂，連兵積年，或遇傾城之敗，覆軍之禍，坑師沈卒，往往而然，孤孫煢子，十室而九。

translations.literal: Since recently the central plain has met ruin and chaos, continuous arms many years, sometimes encountering the defeat of a fallen city, the disaster of an overturned army, pitting armies drowning soldiers—often thus; orphaned grandsons and solitary sons, nine of ten chambers.
translations.idiomatic: For years the Central Plain has been a battlefield of fallen cities and annihilated hosts; sons and grandsons are orphaned in nine houses out of ten.

sentences.zh: 兼三方岳峙，父子異邦，存亡吉凶，杳成天外。

translations.literal: Added to three sides peak-standing like ranges, fathers and sons in different states, survival and perishing, good and ill, dimly become beyond Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Three powers stand like mountain ranges while fathers and sons live under different flags, with no news of whether the other lives or dies.

sentences.zh: 或便假一時，或依嬴博之制，孝子糜身無補，順孫心喪靡及，雖招魂虛葬以敘罔極之情，又禮無招葬之文，令不此載。

translations.literal: Some then borrow for a time, some rely on the system of Ying Bo; filial sons exhaust body without remedy, obedient grandsons' heart-mourning cannot reach; although summoning soul and empty burial to narrate unbounded feeling, again ritual lacks the text of summoning burial, the ordinance does not carry this.
translations.idiomatic: Many must bury in haste or leave kin unburied like the wanderers of old; filial grief cannot set the world right; soul-summoning rites and token burials express love where full funeral is impossible, yet the canon never prescribed such makeshift mourning, and the code is silent.

sentences.zh: 若斯之流，抱琳琅而無申，懷英才而不齒，誠可痛也。

translations.literal: If the like of this stream, embracing fine jade yet without declaration, cherishing outstanding talent yet not ranked—truly can be grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Men who hold talent like jade in the sleeve yet cannot serve the state are a loss worth weeping over.

sentences.zh: 恐非明揚側陋，務盡時珍之道。

translations.literal: I fear it is not the way of bright raising of humble corners, striving to exhaust the season's treasures.
translations.idiomatic: This cannot be the way to "raise the obscure from the side" and gather every worthy the age affords.

sentences.zh: 吳起、二陳之疇，終將無所展其才幹。

translations.literal: The class of Wu Qi and the two Chens, in the end will have nowhere to unfold their talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Wu Qi's or Chen Ping's stamp would never get to show what they can do.

sentences.zh: 漢祖何由免于平城之圍？

translations.literal: How could Han's ancestor thereby avoid the encirclement at Pingcheng?
translations.idiomatic: How would Han Gaozu have escaped the siege at Pingcheng?

sentences.zh: 郅支之首何以懸于漢關？

translations.literal: How did Zhizhi's head thereby hang at the Han pass?
translations.idiomatic: How would Zhizhi's head ever have hung on the Han frontier gate?

sentences.zh: 謹案《戊辰詔書》，蕩清瑕穢，與天下更始，以明惟新之慶。

translations.literal: Respectfully investigating the Wuchen edict, sweeping clear filth and stain, with the world renewing beginning, to clarify the celebration of renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Wuchen edict that washed away guilt and gave the realm a fresh start in the spirit of renewal.

sentences.zh: 五六年間，尋相違伐，於則天之體，臣竊未安。

translations.literal: Within five or six years, seeking each other violated and struck—regarding the body of obeying Heaven, your servant privately is not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within five or six years that policy was reversed and men were punished again—for a government that claims the Mandate of Heaven, I find that unsettling.

sentences.zh: 」俊曰：「煒宿德碩儒，練明刑法，覽其所陳，良足采也。

translations.literal: " Jun said, "Chang Wei is an aged man of cultivated virtue, a great scholar, thorough in penal law; reviewing what he has set forth, truly is sufficient to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun replied, "Chang Wei is a scholar of long standing and a master of statute; his memorial deserves to be followed.

sentences.zh: 今六合未寧，喪亂未已，又正當搜奇拔異之秋，未可才行兼舉，且除此條，聽大同更議。」

translations.literal: Now the six harmonies are not yet tranquil, ruin and chaos not yet ended, again it is just the autumn of searching out the strange and raising the exceptional—not yet able to combine conduct and talent; for the moment remove this article, listen to great concord for later deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still unsettled; this is the very season to seek out hidden talent—not yet time to demand perfection in every virtue. Suspend this clause for now and let the court debate a broader settlement later."

sentences.zh: 使昌黎、遼東二郡營起廆廟，范陽、燕郡構皝廟，以其護軍平熙領將作大匠，監造二廟焉。

translations.literal: He ordered Changli and Liaodong two commanderies to build Gui's temple, Fanyang and Yan commanderies to construct Huang's temple, with his guard general Ping Xi concurrently grand master of works, supervising construction of the two temples.
translations.idiomatic: He directed Changli and Liaodong to raise a shrine to Murong Gui, Fanyang and Yan to build one to Murong Huang, and put his guard general Ping Xi in charge of the works as acting minister.

sentences.zh: 苻堅平州刺史劉特率戶五千降於俊。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's inspector of Pingzhou Liu Te led households five thousand to submit to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's governor of Pingzhou, Liu Te, brought five thousand households over to Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 河間李黑聚眾千餘，攻略州郡，殺棗強令衛顏，俊長樂太守傅顏討斬之。

translations.literal: Hejian Li Hei gathered a host over a thousand, raided and attacked prefectures and commanderies, killed Zaoqiang magistrate Wei Yan; Jun's Changle governor Fu Yan campaigned and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hei of Hejian raised more than a thousand men, pillaged the region, and slew the magistrate of Zaoqiang, Wei Yan; Murong Jun's governor of Changle, Fu Yan, hunted him down and executed him.

sentences.zh: 常山大樹自拔，根下得璧七十、圭七十三，光色精奇，有異常玉。

translations.literal: A great tree in Changshan uprooted itself; beneath the roots were obtained seventy bi and seventy-three gui, light and color refined and strange, different from ordinary jade.
translations.idiomatic: A great tree in Changshan tore itself from the earth; beneath its roots lay seventy disks and seventy-three scepters of jade, glowing with uncanny light unlike common stone.

sentences.zh: 俊以為嶽神之命，遣其尚書郎段勤乙太宰祀之。

translations.literal: Jun considered it the command of the marchmount spirit; he dispatched his masters-of-writing gentleman Duan Qin to sacrifice to it with the grand tailao offering.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun read this as an oracle from the sacred peak and sent his Secretariat clerk Duan Qin to offer the highest-grade sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.

sentences.zh: 初，冉閔之僭號也，石季龍將李曆、張平、高昌等並率其所部稱籓於俊，遣子入侍。

translations.literal: At first, when Ran Min usurped the title, Shi Jilong's generals Li Li, Zhang Ping, Gao Chang and others together led their departments declaring vassalage to Jun, sending sons to attend.
translations.idiomatic: When Ran Min seized the throne, Shi Hu's old generals Li Li, Zhang Ping, Gao Chang, and others had each pledged Yan their allegiance and sent hostages.

sentences.zh: 既而投款建鄴，結援苻堅，並受爵位，羈縻自固，雖貢使不絕，而誠節未盡。

translations.literal: Afterward they cast allegiance to Jianye, tied aid to Fu Jian, and together received ranks and titles, tethered and self-firmed; although tribute envoys did not cease, yet sincere integrity was not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Later they courted Jiankang and allied with Fu Jian, accepting titles from both sides; though their missions never stopped, their loyalty was divided.

sentences.zh: 呂護之走野王也，遣弟奉表謝罪於俊，拜甯南將軍、河內太守。

translations.literal: When Lu Hu fled to Yewang, he dispatched a younger brother to submit a memorial acknowledging guilt to Jun, appointed General Who Pacifies the South, Henei governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Hu fled to Yewang he sent his brother with a letter of submission and was named General Who Pacifies the South and governor of Henei.

sentences.zh: 又上党馮鴦自稱太守，附于張平，平屢言之，俊以平故，赦其罪，以為京兆太守。

translations.literal: Moreover Shangdang Feng Yuan styled himself governor, attached to Zhang Ping; Ping repeatedly spoke of him; Jun because of Ping's sake, pardoned his crime, appointed him Jingzhao governor.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Feng Yuan of Shangdang declared himself governor and leaned on Zhang Ping; Ping interceded repeatedly, and Murong Jun, for Ping's sake, forgave him and named him governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 護、鴦亦陰通京師。

translations.literal: Hu and Yuan also secretly communicated with the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hu and Feng Yuan were also in secret contact with the Jin court.

sentences.zh: 張平跨有新興、雁門、西河、太原、上黨、上郡之地，壘壁三百餘，胡晉十餘萬戶，遂拜置征、鎮，為鼎峙之勢。

translations.literal: Zhang Ping straddling possessed Xinxing, Yanmen, Xihe, Taiyuan, Shangdang, and Shang commanderies' territory, more than three hundred ramparts, Hu and Jin more than a hundred thousand households, thereupon appointed and installed expedition and garrison commanders, forming tripod-standoff momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ping held a belt of territory across Xinxing, Yanmen, Xihe, Taiyuan, Shangdang, and Shang—over three hundred fortified camps and a hundred thousand Hu and Chinese households—and handed out expedition and garrison titles until he stood like a third leg of a tripod.

sentences.zh: 俊其司徒慕容評討平，領軍慕輿根討鴦，司空陽騖討昌，撫軍慕容臧攻曆。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jun's minister of education Murong Ping campaigned against Ping, leader of the army Moyu Gen campaigned against Yuan, minister of works Yang Wu campaigned against Chang, general Who Pacifies the Army Murong Zang attacked Li.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun sent his minister Murong Ping against Zhang Ping, his marshal Moyu Gen against Feng Yuan, his minister of works Yang Wu against Gao Chang, and his general Murong Zang against Li Li.

sentences.zh: 并州壘壁降者百餘所，以尚書右僕射悅綰為安西將軍、領護匈奴中郎將、并州刺史以撫之。

translations.literal: In Bing more than a hundred ramparts submitted; he appointed right supervisor of the masters of writing Yue Wan as General Who Pacifies the West, concurrent protector of the Xiongnu center commandant, and inspector of Bing to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred Bingzhou strongholds capitulated; Murong Jun named Yue Wan General Who Pacifies the West, concurrent Xiongnu commandant, and governor of Bing to settle the region.

sentences.zh: 平所署征西諸葛驤、鎮北蘇象、甯東喬庶、鎮南石賢等率壘壁百三十八降於俊，俊大悅，皆復其官爵。

translations.literal: Ping's appointed west-expedition Zhuge Xiang, north-garrison Su Xiang, east-pacification Qiao Shu, south-garrison Shi Xian and others led one hundred thirty-eight ramparts to submit to Jun; Jun was greatly pleased, all restored their offices and noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ping's officers Zhuge Xiang, Su Xiang, Qiao Shu, Shi Xian, and others brought a hundred thirty-eight forts over to Yan; Murong Jun restored every man's rank and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 既而平率眾三千奔於平陽，鴦奔于野王，曆走滎陽，昌奔邵陵，悉降其眾。

translations.literal: Afterward Ping led a host of three thousand and fled to Pingyang; Yuan fled to Yewang; Li fled to Xingyang; Chang fled to Shaoling; all submitted their hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ping then bolted to Pingyang with three thousand men; Feng Yuan, Li Li, and Gao Chang scattered to Yewang, Xingyang, and Shaoling, each yielding his troops.

sentences.zh: 俊於是復圖入寇，兼欲經略關西，乃令州郡校閱見丁，精覆隱漏，率戶留一丁，餘悉發之，欲使步卒滿一百五十萬，期明年大集，將進臨洛陽，為三方節度。

translations.literal: Jun thereupon again planned entry invasion, also wished to manage the west of the passes; thereupon ordered prefectures and commanderies to review visible adult males, strictly cover hidden and leaked, per household retaining one adult male, the rest all drafted, desiring to make infantry fill 1,500,000, setting next year great assembly, about to advance and face Luoyang, as three-side regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun then planned another drive south and a campaign in Guanzhong: he ordered every district to muster every able man, hunt down draft evaders, leave only one male per household at home, and call up the rest until he could field one and a half million foot, with a full muster at Ye the next winter before marching on Luoyang on three axes.

sentences.zh: 武邑劉貴上書極諫，陳百姓凋弊，召兵非法，恐人不堪命，有土崩之禍，並陳時政不便於時者十有三事。

translations.literal: Wuyi's Liu Gui submitted a memorial urgently remonstrating, stating the hundred surnames withered and exhausted, calling soldiers not according to law, fearing people could not bear the command, having earth-collapse misfortune, together stating current government thirteen matters not convenient to the age.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui of Wuyi sent a blunt memorial: the people were ruined, the levy lawless, and such demands risked collapse; he added thirteen practical reforms.

sentences.zh: 俊覽而悅之，付公卿博議，事多納用，乃改為三五占兵，寬戎備一周，悉令明年季冬赴集鄴都。

translations.literal: Jun examined it and was pleased with it, handed it to dukes and ministers for broad deliberation; matters mostly were adopted and used, thereupon changed to three-fifths draft soldiers, widened garrison preparation one cycle, entirely ordered next year's last month of winter to go assemble at the capital Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun welcomed it, sent it round the high ministers, and adopted most of his advice—scaling the draft to one man in three, easing garrison rotations by a year, and fixing the great muster for the twelfth month at Ye.

sentences.zh: 是歲，晉將荀羨攻山茌，拔之。

translations.literal: That year, Jin general Xun Xian attacked Shanci and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The same year Jin's Xun Xian stormed and took Shanci.

sentences.zh: 斬俊太山太守賈堅。

translations.literal: He beheaded Jun's Taishan governor Jia Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Murong Jun's governor of Taishan, Jia Jian.

sentences.zh: 俊青州刺史慕容塵遣司馬悅明救之，羨師敗績，復陷山茌。

translations.literal: Jun's inspector of Qingzhou Murong Chen dispatched Major Yue Ming to rescue them; Xian's army was defeated in the reckoning, again lost Shanci.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chen, Murong Jun's governor of Qingzhou, sent Yue Ming to relieve the town, but Xun Xian rallied, broke the Yan column, and retook Shanci.

sentences.zh: 俊立小學於顯賢裏以教胄子。

translations.literal: Jun established a minor school at Xianxian ward to teach scions.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun opened a primary school in Xianxian ward for the sons of the nobility.

sentences.zh: 封其子泓為濟北王，沖為中山王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed his son Hong as Prince of Jibei, Chong as Prince of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He created his sons Murong Hong and Murong Chong princes of Jibei and Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 宴群臣于蒲池，酒酣，賦詩，因談經史，語及周太子晉，潸然流涕，顧謂群臣曰：「昔魏武追痛倉舒，孫權悼登無已，孤常謂二主緣愛稱奇，無大雅之體。

translations.literal: He feasted the host of ministers at Pu Pool; when wine was deep, he composed poetry, thereupon discussed classics and histories; speech reached Zhou crown prince Jin, tears flowing; he turned and said to the host of ministers, "In the past Wei Wu pursued grief for Cangshu, Sun Quan mourned Deng without end—I always said the two lords because of love called it strange, without the great ya's deportment.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet by Pu Pool, flushed with wine, Murong Jun turned to history, came to Prince Jin of Zhou, and wept. He told his ministers, "I used to think Cao Cao's grief for Cao Chong and Sun Quan's endless mourning for Sun Deng were mere doting fathers, not the bearing of high kings.

sentences.zh: 自曄亡以來，孤鬚髮中白，始知二主有以而然。

translations.literal: Since Ye's death, in the midst of my whiskers and hair I have turned white; I begin to know the two lords had reason thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Since Murong Ye died my beard has gone grey; now I see those fathers had cause after all.

sentences.zh: 卿等言曄定何如也？

translations.literal: You gentlemen speak—how was Ye settled?
translations.idiomatic: Tell me honestly—what manner of heir was Murong Ye?

sentences.zh: 孤今悼之，得無貽怪將來乎？

translations.literal: I now mourn him—must I not hand down blame to the future?
translations.idiomatic: If I indulge this grief, will posterity fault me for it?

sentences.zh: 」其司徒左長史李績對曰：「獻懷之在東宮，臣為中庶子，既忝近侍，聖質志業，臣實不敢不知。

translations.literal: " His minister of education left chief clerk Li Ji replied, "When Xianhuai was in the Eastern Palace, your servant was palace attendant; having disgraced near attendance, the sage substance and aims and enterprise, your servant truly did not dare not to know.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji, chief clerk of the ministry, answered, "When the late crown prince lived in the Eastern Palace, I served as his gentleman attendant; I could not fail to know his character and pursuits.

sentences.zh: 臣聞道備無愆，其唯聖人乎。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: the way complete without fault—perhaps only the sage?
translations.idiomatic: They say only the perfectly wise never stumble.

sentences.zh: 先太子大德有八，未見闕也。

translations.literal: The former crown prince's great virtues were eight; I have not seen deficiency.
translations.idiomatic: The late heir had eight great virtues; I saw no fatal flaw in him.

sentences.zh: 」俊曰：「卿言亦以過矣，然試言之。

translations.literal: " Jun said, "Your words also are excessive, yet try to speak them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun said, "You flatter him, but list the eight all the same.

sentences.zh: 」績言：「至孝自天，性與道合，此其一也。

translations.literal: " Ji spoke: "Supreme filiality from Heaven, nature joined with the Way—this is the first.
translations.idiomatic: Ji began: "First, inborn filial piety that matched the Way.

sentences.zh: 聰敏慧悟，機思若流，此其二也。

translations.literal: Clever and keen, wise and awakened, stratagem and thought like flowing—this is the second.
translations.idiomatic: Second, quick wit and ideas that flowed like water.

sentences.zh: 沈毅好斷，理詣無幽，此其三也。

translations.literal: Deep and resolute, fond of deciding, principle reaching without dark—this is the third.
translations.idiomatic: Third, depth and resolve—he grasped every issue to the root.

sentences.zh: 疾諛亮物，雅悅直言，此其四也。

translations.literal: Hating flattery, brightening things, elegantly pleased with straight speech—this is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, he hated sycophants and welcomed blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 好學愛賢，不恥下問，此其五也。

translations.literal: Fond of study, loving the worthy, not ashamed to ask those below—this is the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, he loved learning and sought advice from humbler men without shame.

sentences.zh: 英姿邁古，藝業超時，此其六也。

translations.literal: Heroic bearing surpassing antiquity, arts and enterprise exceeding the age—this is the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, a heroic presence that outshone his age.

sentences.zh: 虛襟恭讓，尊師重道，此其七也。

translations.literal: Empty bosom, respectful yielding, honoring teachers, weighting the Way—this is the seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, humility and reverence for teachers and the Way.

sentences.zh: 輕財好施，勤恤民隱，此其八也。

translations.literal: Lightening wealth, fond of giving, diligently caring for the people's hardships—this is the eighth.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, open purse for charity and care for the common people's woes.

sentences.zh: 」俊泣曰：「卿雖褒譽，然此兒若在，吾死無憂也。
