translations.literal: " Jun wept, saying, "Although you praise and extol, yet if this child were still here, I would have no worry in death.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun wept, "Even allowing your praise—had that son lived, I could face death untroubled.

sentences.zh: 吾既不能追蹤唐、虞，官天下以禪有德，近模三王，以世傳授。

translations.literal: I already am unable to track Tang and Yu, officializing All under Heaven to yield to the virtuous; near modeling the three kings, by generations transmitting and entrusting.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot rival Tang and Yu and yield the realm to the worthiest; like later dynasties I must pass the throne by blood.

sentences.zh: 景茂幼沖，器藝未舉，卿以為何如？

translations.literal: Jingmao is young and slight, vessels and arts not yet raised—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jingmao is a child, his talents untried—what say you?

sentences.zh: 」績曰：「皇太子天資岐嶷，聖敬日躋，而八闃然，二闕未補，雅好游田，娛心絲竹，所以為損耳。

translations.literal: " Ji said, "The imperial heir by Heaven's endowment is keen and upright, sage reverence daily climbing, yet eight are silent, two are not mended—he elegantly loves roaming and hunting, entertaining heart with silk and bamboo—this is what is detriment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji answered, "The crown prince is bright and reverent, yet two of the eight virtues are wanting—he loves the hunt and music too well; that is the flaw.

sentences.zh: 」俊顧謂暐曰：「伯陽之言，藥石之惠，汝宜戢之。

translations.literal: " Jun turned and said to Wei, "Boyang's words are the benefit of medicine and stone; you should gather them in.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun turned to Murong Wei and said, "Treat Li Ji's counsel like medicine—take it to heart.

sentences.zh: 」因問高年疾苦、孤寡不能自存者，賜穀帛有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon he asked the aged about illness and suffering, orphans and widows unable to preserve themselves, bestowing grain and silk each according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked after the sick elderly and destitute widows and orphans, granting grain and cloth by need.

sentences.zh: 俊夜夢石季龍齧其臂，寤而惡之，命發其墓，剖棺出屍，蹋而罵之曰：「死胡安敢夢生天子！

translations.literal: Jun at night dreamed Shi Jilong bit his arm; waking he hated it, ordered opening his tomb, splitting the coffin and bringing out the corpse, trampled and reviled him, saying, "Dead Hu how dare you dream the living Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun dreamed Shi Hu bit his arm; he woke in fury, had Shi Hu's tomb opened, the corpse dragged out, trampled, and shouted at—"How dare a dead barbarian haunt a living emperor!

sentences.zh: 」遣其御史中尉陽約數其殘酷之罪，鞭之，棄于漳水。

translations.literal: " He dispatched his censor-in-chief Yang Yue to enumerate his cruel crimes, whipped him, and cast him into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yang Yue, his censor-in-chief, to recite Shi Hu's crimes, had the corpse flogged, and threw it in the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 諸葛攸又率水陸三萬討俊，入自石門，屯於河渚。

translations.literal: Zhuge You again led thirty thousand by water and land to punish Jun, entering from Stone Gate, encamped at the river islet.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge You took thirty thousand men by land and water through Stone Gate and camped on a mid-river shoal.

sentences.zh: 攸部將匡超進據嵪㠂，蕭館屯於新柵，又遣督護徐冏率水軍三千泛舟上下，為東西聲勢。

translations.literal: You's lieutenant Kuang Chao advanced and occupied the Qiao'ai heights, Xiao Guan encamped at New Palisade; again dispatched overseer Xu Jiong leading three thousand water army floating boats up and down, making east-west momentum.
translations.idiomatic: His officers Kuang Chao seized the Qiao'ai heights, Xiao Guan built a new stockade, and Xu Jiong patrolled three thousand boats upriver and down to screen both flanks.

sentences.zh: 俊遣慕容評、傅顏等統步騎五萬，戰于東阿，王師敗績。

translations.literal: Jun dispatched Murong Ping, Fu Yan and others commanding fifty thousand infantry and cavalry, battled at Dong'e; the royal army was defeated in the reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping and Fu Yan met them at Dong'e with fifty thousand men and shattered the Jin army.

sentences.zh: 塞北七國賀蘭、涉勒等皆降。

translations.literal: North of the passes seven states Helan, Shele and others all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Seven northern tribes including Helan and Shele submitted.

sentences.zh: 俄而俊寢疾，謂慕容恪曰：「吾所疾惙然，當恐不濟。

translations.literal: Shortly Jun lay ill; he said to Murong Ke, "My illness is suddenly such—I fear I will not cross over.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Murong Jun took to his bed and told Murong Ke, "This sickness has come on fast; I may not recover.

sentences.zh: 修短命也，復何所恨！

translations.literal: As for my short life—what again is there to resent!
translations.idiomatic: A short life is my lot—what more is there to regret?

sentences.zh: 但二寇未除，景茂沖幼，慮其未堪多難。

translations.literal: Only the two bandits are not yet removed; Jingmao is young and slight; I worry he cannot yet bear many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jin and Qin still stand unconquered, and Jingmao is a child—I fear he is not ready for such trials.

sentences.zh: 吾欲遠追宋宣，以社稷屬汝。

translations.literal: I desire distantly to track Song Xuan, to entrust the altars of soil and grain to you.
translations.idiomatic: I would follow Duke Xuan of Song and leave the altars of state in your hands.

sentences.zh: 」恪曰：「太子雖幼，天縱聰聖，必能勝殘刑措，不可以亂正統也。

translations.literal: " Ke said, "Although the crown prince is young, Heaven has endowed him clever and sage; he will surely be able to overcome cruelty and set aside punishments—one may not by this disorder the orthodox succession.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke said, "The heir is young, yet Heaven has made him wise; he will grow able to soften harsh ways—do not disturb the legitimate line of succession.

sentences.zh: 」俊怒曰：「兄弟之間豈虛飾也！

translations.literal: " Jun angrily said, "Between brothers how can there be empty ornament!
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun snapped, "Between brothers we do not trade empty compliments!"

sentences.zh: 」恪曰：「陛下若以臣堪荷天下之任者，寧不能輔少主乎！

translations.literal: " Ke said, "If Your Majesty considers your servant able to shoulder All under Heaven's burden, how could I be unable to assist the young lord!
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke answered, "If you think I can carry the realm, you know I will serve the boy emperor faithfully.

sentences.zh: 」俊曰：「若汝行周公之事，吾復何憂！

translations.literal: " Jun said, "If you perform the Duke of Zhou's affairs, what again would I worry!
translations.idiomatic: If you act as the Duke of Zhou did, I have nothing left to fear."

sentences.zh: 李績清方忠亮，堪任大事，汝善遇之。」

translations.literal: Li Ji is pure, square, loyal, and bright, able to shoulder great affairs—you should treat him well."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji is upright, loyal, and fit for great responsibility—cherish him."

sentences.zh: 是時兵集鄴城，盜賊互起，每夜攻劫，晨昏斷行。

translations.literal: At that time troops had assembled at Ye city; bandits and thieves mutually arose; each night raiding and plundering, morning and dusk cutting off travel.
translations.idiomatic: With the host massed at Ye, banditry flared; night raids made the roads unsafe from dusk to dawn.

sentences.zh: 於是寬常賦，設奇禁，賊盜有相告者賜奉車都尉，捕誅賊首木穀和等百餘人，乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he widened the regular tax, established strange prohibitions; for bandits and thieves there was mutual informing—he bestowed chariot commandant; capturing and executing bandit chiefs Mu Guhe and others more than a hundred persons, then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun eased ordinary taxes, posted special edicts, offered the rank of chariot commandant for informers, and executed over a hundred ringleaders such as Mu Guhe until order returned.

sentences.zh: ，俊死，時年四十二，在位十一年。

translations.literal: Jun died; at that time forty-two years old, on the throne eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun died at the age of forty-two, having reigned eleven years.

sentences.zh: 偽諡景昭皇帝，廟號烈祖，墓號龍陵。

translations.literal: False posthumous title Emperor Jingzhao, temple name Liezu, tomb name Dragon Mound.
translations.idiomatic: He received the temple name Liezu, the posthumous title Emperor Jingzhao, and was buried at the Longling mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 俊雅好文籍，自初即位至末年，講論不倦，覽政之暇，唯與侍臣錯綜義理，凡所著述四十餘篇。

translations.literal: Jun elegantly loved documents and records; from first ascending the throne to the final year, lecturing and discussing without weariness; in the gaps of reviewing government, only with attendant ministers interweaving principles of meaning—altogether what he composed was more than forty pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun loved books from his accession to his death, debated the classics without tiring, and in spare moments from government worked through doctrine with his intimates—leaving more than forty writings.

sentences.zh: 性嚴重，慎威儀，未曾以慢服臨朝，雖閒居宴處亦無懈怠之色雲。

translations.literal: By nature strict and weighty, cautious of awe-inspiring deportment, never with slovenly dress facing court; although in idle residence feasting and dwelling, there was also no slackness in expression—it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave by nature, careful of dignity, never came to court in undress, and even in private showed no slack bearing—or so it is recorded.

sentences.zh: 韓恆

translations.literal: Han Heng (personal name, section heading).
translations.idiomatic: Han Heng

sentences.zh: 韓恆，字景山，灌津人也。

translations.literal: Han Heng, courtesy name Jingshan, was a man of Guanjin.
translations.idiomatic: Han Heng, styled Jingshan, was a native of Guanjin.

sentences.zh: 父默，以學行顯名。

translations.literal: His father Mo, by learning and conduct displayed name.
translations.idiomatic: His father Han Mo was known for scholarship and character.

sentences.zh: 恆少能屬文，師事同郡張載，載奇之，曰：「王佐才也。

translations.literal: Heng in youth was able to compose texts; he studied serving same commandery Zhang Zai; Zai thought him strange, saying, "Wang-zuo talent.
translations.idiomatic: Han Heng wrote well in youth and studied under Zhang Zai of his commandery; Zhang Zai exclaimed that he had the makings of a king's minister.

sentences.zh: 」身長八尺一寸，博覽經籍，無所不通。

translations.literal: " His body was eight chi one cun in height; he broadly examined the classics and records; nothing he did not penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet one inch tall, read widely, and mastered every field he touched.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，避地遼東。

translations.literal: At the Yongjia turmoil, he avoided trouble in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongjia catastrophe struck, he fled to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 廆既逐崔毖，復徙昌黎，召見，嘉之，拜參軍事。

translations.literal: After Gui had expelled Cui Bi, again moved to Changli, summoned and saw him, praised him, appointed him adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Gui drove out Cui Bi and moved the seat to Changli, he received Han Heng, praised him, and named him an army adviser.

sentences.zh: 咸和中，宋該等建議以廆立功一隅，勤誠王室，位卑任重，不足以鎮華夷，宜表請大將軍、燕王之號。

translations.literal: In the Xianhe years, Song Gai and others proposed that Gui had accomplished merit in one corner, diligent and sincere to the royal house, position low burden heavy, not sufficient to awe Chinese and barbarians; it was fitting to memorialize requesting the grand general and Prince of Yan titles.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianhe, Song Gai and others argued that Murong Gui's loyalty to Jin from the frontier merited the titles grand general and Prince of Yan, for his low rank could not overawe Hu and Chinese alike.

sentences.zh: 廆納之，命群僚博議，咸以為宜如該議。

translations.literal: Gui accepted it, ordered the host of officials broadly to deliberate; all thought it fitting to act as Gai's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gui agreed, put the question to his officials, and they unanimously backed Song Gai's plan.

sentences.zh: 恆駁曰：「自群胡乘間，人嬰荼毒，諸夏蕭條，無復綱紀。

translations.literal: Heng refuted, saying, "Since the various Hu seized the opportunity, people encountered bitter poison; the various Xia were desolate, no longer having guideline and cord.
translations.idiomatic: Han Heng objected: "Since the barbarian uprisings the people have suffered and the heartland lies in ruins—there is no longer a proper order.

sentences.zh: 明公忠武篤誠，憂勤社稷，抗節孤危之中，建功萬里之外，終古勤王之義，未之有也。

translations.literal: The enlightened lord is loyal, martial, and sincere, anxious and diligent for the altars of soil and grain, resisting the norm in solitary peril within, establishing merit beyond ten thousand li—through antiquity the righteousness of diligent kingship to the Zhou house, there has never been such.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have been loyal, martial, and true, toiling for the altars amid peril and winning glory a thousand leagues from the court—such service to the house of Jin is without precedent.

sentences.zh: 夫立功者患信義不著，不患名位不高，故桓文有甯復一匡之功，亦不先求禮命以令諸侯。

translations.literal: As for one who establishes merit, he worries trust and righteousness are not displayed, not worries name and position are not high; therefore Huan and Wen had the merit of restoring and unifying, yet did not first seek ritual commands to order the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Those who build greatness fear only that good faith will not show, not that rank is too low; Duke Huan and Duke Wen restored the realm without first demanding ceremonial investiture over the lords.

sentences.zh: 宜繕甲兵，候機會，除群凶，靖四海，功成之後，九錫自至。

translations.literal: It is fitting to repair armor and weapons, await opportunity and meeting, eliminate the various fierce, quiet the four seas; after merit is accomplished, the nine bestowals will arrive of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Repair arms, watch the moment, sweep away the wicked, and pacify the realm—the nine honors will come in their own time once merit is plain.

sentences.zh: 且要君以求寵爵者，非為臣之義也。

translations.literal: Moreover demanding favor from the ruler to seek ennobling rank is not the righteousness of serving as minister.
translations.idiomatic: To squeeze titles from one's sovereign is not the way of a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 」廆不平之，出為新昌令。

translations.literal: " Gui was not pleased with it, sent him out as magistrate of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gui took offense and sent him out as magistrate of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 皝為鎮軍，復參軍事。

translations.literal: When Huang was General Who Guards the Army, again [Heng] joined the army staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Huang became General Who Guards the Army, Han Heng again joined his staff.

sentences.zh: 遷營丘太守，政化大行。

translations.literal: He was promoted Yingqiu governor; government transformation greatly proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Yingqiu, where his rule transformed the region.

sentences.zh: 俊為大將軍，徵拜諮議參軍，加揚烈將軍。

translations.literal: When Jun was grand general, he summoned and appointed him consulting adjutant, added General Who Displays Ferocity.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Jun became grand general, he recalled Han Heng as advisory adviser with the added title General Who Displays Ferocity.

sentences.zh: 俊僭位，將定五行次，眾論紛紜。

translations.literal: When Jun usurped the throne, about to fix the five phases' sequence, the host of opinions was tangled and diverse.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Jun took the imperial title, the court wrangled over which phase the Yan line should claim.

sentences.zh: 恆時疾在龍城，俊召恆以決之。

translations.literal: Heng at the time was ill in Longcheng; Jun summoned Heng to decide it.
translations.idiomatic: Han Heng lay ill in Longcheng, but Murong Jun summoned him to settle the question.

sentences.zh: 恆未至而群臣議以燕宜承晉為水德。

translations.literal: Before Heng arrived, the host of ministers deliberated that Yan fittingly should succeed Jin as water virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Before Han Heng arrived, the ministers voted that Yan should follow Jin as the water phase.

sentences.zh: 既而恆至，言於俊曰：「趙有中原，非唯人事，天所命也。

translations.literal: Afterward Heng arrived, spoke to Jun, saying, "Zhao held the central plain—not only human affairs, Heaven commanded it.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Heng came, he told Murong Jun, "Former Zhao held the Central Plain by Heaven's appointment, not by human whim alone.

sentences.zh: 天實與之，而人奪之，臣竊謂不可。

translations.literal: Heaven truly gave it, yet people seized it—your servant privately considers this impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gave that mandate to Zhao; for us to snatch their succession token strikes me as wrong.

sentences.zh: 且大燕王跡始自于震，于《易》，震為青龍。

translations.literal: Moreover Great Yan's kingly traces began from the Zhen trigram; in the Changes, Zhen is the green dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Great Yan's royal omens began under the Zhen trigram—the Azure Dragon of the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 受命之初，有龍見於都邑城，龍為木德，幽契之符也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of receiving the mandate, there was a dragon appearing at the capital district wall; the dragon is wood virtue—a sign secretly matching the You region.
translations.idiomatic: When the mandate first dawned, a dragon appeared at the capital—dragons belong to the wood phase, the sign that fits Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 」俊初雖難改，後終從恆議。

translations.literal: " Jun at first although found it hard to change, afterward in the end followed Heng's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun resisted at first but finally adopted Han Heng's argument.

sentences.zh: 俊秘書監清河聶熊聞恆言，乃歎曰：「不有君子，國何以興，其韓令君之謂乎！

translations.literal: Jun's secretary supervisor Qinghe Nie Xiong heard Heng's words, then sighed, saying, "Without a gentleman, how could the state rise—this probably speaks of Director Han!
translations.idiomatic: Nie Xiong, prefect of the palace writers, heard Han Heng and sighed, "Without such men a state cannot flourish—he meant Han Heng."

sentences.zh: 」後與李產俱傅東宮，從太子曄入朝，俊顧謂左右曰：「此二傅一代偉人，未易繼也。

translations.literal: " Later with Li Chan together tutored the Eastern Palace, following crown prince Ye entering court; Jun turned and said to left and right, "These two tutors are generation's great men—not easy to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Li Chan tutored the Eastern Palace. When they entered court with Crown Prince Murong Ye, Murong Jun murmured, "Two tutors of that stature will not easily be replaced.

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: " He was thus esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the regard in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 李產

translations.literal: Li Chan (personal name, section heading).
translations.idiomatic: Li Chan

sentences.zh: 李產，字子喬，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Chan, courtesy name Ziqiao, was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chan, styled Ziqiao, came from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 少剛厲，有志格。

translations.literal: In youth he was firm and severe, had aspiration and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was stern and high-minded.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，同郡祖逖擁眾部于南土，力能自固，產遂往依之。

translations.literal: At the Yongjia turmoil, same commandery Zu Ti gathered a host and garrisoned in the southern lands, strength able to self-firm; Chan thereupon went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongjia disaster Zu Ti of his commandery had carved out a southern base; Li Chan went to join him.

sentences.zh: 逖素好從橫，弟約有大志，產微知其旨，乃率子弟十數人間行還鄉里，仕于石氏，為本郡太守。

translations.literal: Ti by nature was fond of vertical and horizontal schemes; younger brother Yue had great aims; Chan subtly knew their intention, thereupon led sons and younger brothers more than ten persons by byways returning to home village, served the Shi clan, became governor of his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti loved grand strategy and his brother Zu Yue harbored larger designs; Li Chan sensed their drift, slipped home with a dozen kinsmen, and took office under the Shi regime as governor of his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 及慕容俊南征，前鋒達郡界，鄉人皆勸產降，產曰：「夫受人之祿，當同其安危，今若舍此節以圖存，義士將謂我何！

translations.literal: When Murong Jun southern-campaigned, the van reached the commandery border; fellow villagers all urged Chan to submit; Chan said, "As for receiving another's salary, one should share his safety and danger; now if I cast aside this integrity to seek preservation, what will righteous men say of me!
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Jun marched south and his vanguard reached the border, his neighbors urged surrender, but Li Chan said, "I took Shi Hu's pay—I must share his fortune; if I discard my duty to save myself, what would men of honor think?

sentences.zh: 」眾潰，始詣軍請降。

translations.literal: The host scattered; only then did he go to the army requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Shi Hu's host collapsed did he present himself to the Yan army and yield.

sentences.zh: 俊嘲之曰：「卿受石氏寵任，衣錦本鄉，何故不能立功于時，而反委質乎！

translations.literal: Jun mocked him, saying, "You received the Shi's favor and appointment, wore brocade in your home village—why could you not establish merit in the season, yet instead cast your substance?
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun taunted him: "You enjoyed Shi Hu's favor and paraded brocade in your home town—why did you never earn your keep until the cause was lost?

sentences.zh: 烈士處身于世，固當如是邪？

translations.literal: A stalwart placing himself in the world—should it solidly be thus?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how a hero serves the times?

sentences.zh: 」產泣曰：「誠知天命有歸，非微臣所抗。

translations.literal: " Chan wept, saying, "I truly know Heaven's mandate has a return, not a petty minister can resist.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chan wept, "I know Heaven's mandate had passed from Shi—I could not fight it.

sentences.zh: 然犬馬為主，豈忘自效，但以孤窮勢蹙，致力無術，[ＦＣ]俛歸死，實非誠款。

translations.literal: Yet dog and horse serving the lord—how could I forget self-effort; only because solitary and pressed, situation urgent, exerting strength without art, bowing head awaiting death—truly was not sincere allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet like a dog or horse I served my master and would have fought on; I was alone, cornered, powerless, forced to bow my head and await death—that was not willing treason.

sentences.zh: 」俊嘉其慷慨，顧謂左右曰：「此真長者也。

translations.literal: " Jun praised his forthright spirit, turned and said to left and right, "This is truly an elder.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun admired his candor and said to his attendants, "This is a man of true integrity.

sentences.zh: 」乃擢用之，歷位尚書。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he raised and employed him, passing through posts to masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He then employed him until Li Chan rose to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 性剛正，好直言，每至進見，未曾不論朝政之得失，同輩咸憚焉，俊亦敬其儒雅。

translations.literal: By nature firm and upright, fond of straight speech; each time reaching advance audience, never did not discuss court government's gains and losses; peers all feared him; Jun also respected his ru elegance.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt and outspoken at every audience, dissecting policy without fear; colleagues dreaded him, yet Murong Jun honored his scholar's bearing.

sentences.zh: 前後固辭年老，不堪理劇。

translations.literal: Before and after he firmly declined because of old age, unable to bear managing severity.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he cited age and refused the crushing burden of office.

sentences.zh: 轉拜太子太保。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed grand guardian of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was then named grand guardian to the heir apparent, an honorific sinceure.

sentences.zh: 謂子績曰：「以吾之才而致於此，始者之願亦已過矣，不可復以西夕之年取笑於來今也。

translations.literal: He spoke to son Ji, saying, "By my talents having reached here, from the first my wishes were already surpassed; I cannot again in west-dusk years invite laughter from present and future.
translations.idiomatic: He told his son Li Ji, "My meager gifts have already taken me farther than I dreamed; I will not spend my twilight years inviting ridicule from the world.

sentences.zh: 」固辭而歸，死於家。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined and returned, died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned for good, went home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 子績。

translations.literal: Son Ji (subsection heading).
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji

sentences.zh: 績字伯陽，少以風節知名，清辯有辭理。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Boyang, in youth by manner and integrity was known, clear in debate and had phrase principle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji, styled Boyang, was known in youth for high principle, lucid argument, and well-ordered speech.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為郡功曹。

translations.literal: At weak crown he was commandery merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he became merit clerk of his commandery.

sentences.zh: 時石季龍親征段遼，師次范陽，百姓饑儉，軍供有闕。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Jilong personally campaigned against Duan Liao; the army halted at Fanyang; the hundred surnames were hungry and lean; army supplies had shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu marched in person against Duan Liao, his host stopped at Fanyang; the people were starving and the commissariat ran short.

sentences.zh: 季龍大怒，大守惶怖避匿。

translations.literal: Jilong was greatly angered; the grand governor in fear and terror hid.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu flew into a rage, and the governor fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 績進曰：「郡帶北裔，與寇接攘，疆埸之間，人懷危慮。

translations.literal: Ji advanced saying, "The commandery girds the northern border, adjoins and rubs the bandits; between border fields, people harbor perilous worry.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji stepped forward: "This commandery lies on the northern frontier cheek-by-jowl with the enemy; every soul along the border lives in dread.

sentences.zh: 聞輿駕親戎，將除殘賊，雖嬰兒白首，咸思效命，非唯為國，亦自求寧，雖身膏草野，猶甘為之，敢有私吝而闕軍實！

translations.literal: " Hearing the imperial chariot personally takes arms, about to eliminate the cruel bandits—although infants and white-haired, all think to devote their lives—not only for the state, also themselves seeking peace; although body greases the grass wilds, still gladly would do it—how dare there be private stinginess and lack army substance!
translations.idiomatic: "When word spread that Your Majesty would lead the host in person to destroy the rebels, every man from babes to greybeards wished to give his life—not for the state alone but to win peace; they would gladly die in the field—who would stint the army out of selfishness?

sentences.zh: 但此年災儉，家有菜色，困弊力屈，無所取濟，逋廢之罪，情在可矜。

translations.literal: Only this year disaster and lean; families have vegetable color; exhausted and bent, strength bent, nothing from which to obtain relief—the crime of delay and default, the feeling lies in what may be pitied.
translations.idiomatic: But this is a year of famine; faces show the green tinge of hunger; folk are drained and cannot scrape up supplies—default is pitiable, not criminal.

sentences.zh: 」季龍見績年少有壯節，嘉而恕之，於是太守獲免。

translations.literal: " Jilong saw Ji was young and had stalwart integrity, praised and pardoned him; thereupon the governor obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu saw the youth's courage, praised him, and relented, and the governor was spared.

sentences.zh: 刺史王午辟為主簿。

translations.literal: Inspector Wang Wu summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The regional inspector Wang Wu named him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 俊之南征也，隨午奔魯口。

translations.literal: When Jun southern-campaigned, he followed Wang Wu fleeing to Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Jun marched south, Li Ji followed Wang Wu to Lukou.

sentences.zh: 鄧恆謂午曰：「績鄉里在北，父已降燕，今雖在此，終不為用，方為人患。

translations.literal: Deng Heng said to Wu, "Ji's village and home are in the north; his father has already submitted to Yan; now although he is here, in the end he will not be used—will become a man's disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Heng warned Wang Wu, "Li Ji's home lies in the north and his father has gone over to Yan; keeping him here serves no good—he will only become a liability.

sentences.zh: 」午曰：「績於喪亂之中捐家立義，情節之重，有侔古烈，若懷嫌害之，必駭眾望。

translations.literal: " Wu said, "Ji in the midst of ruin and chaos cast aside family to establish righteousness; the weight of feeling and integrity has parity with ancient fierceness; if harboring suspicion and harming him, must startle the host of hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wu replied, "In the chaos Li Ji left his kin to stand on principle—his loyalty rivals the heroes of old; to kill him on suspicion would shock every man's conscience.

sentences.zh: 」恆乃止。

translations.literal: " Heng thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Heng dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 午恐績終為恆所害，乃資遣之。

translations.literal: Wu feared Ji in the end would be harmed by Heng, thereupon supplied and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Deng Heng would still murder Li Ji, Wang Wu gave him travel funds and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 及到，俊責其背親後至，績答曰：「臣聞豫讓報智伯仇，稱于前史。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Jun reproached him for betraying kin and arriving late; Ji replied, saying, "Your servant has heard Yurang avenged Lord Zhi's enmity, praised in former histories.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Murong Jun, the emperor rebuked him for belatedly abandoning his kin. Li Ji answered, "Yurang avenged Zhi Bo and won the historians' praise.

sentences.zh: 既官身所在，何事非君！

translations.literal: Since official body is where it is, what affair is not lord!
translations.idiomatic: Wherever a man holds office, whoever sits the throne is his prince.

sentences.zh: 陛下方弘唐、虞之化，臣實未謂歸順之晚也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just now enlarging Tang and Yu's transformation; your servant truly does not consider returning to allegiance late.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now spreads the humane rule of Tang and Yu; I do not think I came too late to submit.

sentences.zh: 」俊曰：「此亦事主之一節耳。

translations.literal: " Jun said, "This also is one node of serving a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun said, "That too is one way to serve a master.

sentences.zh: 」累遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: " He cumulatively was promoted to crown prince palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to gentleman attendant of the palace to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及暐立，慕容恪欲以績為尚書右僕射，暐憾績往言，不許。

translations.literal: When Wei was established, Murong Ke wished to make Ji right supervisor of the masters of writing; Wei resented Ji's former words, did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Wei came to the throne, Murong Ke wanted Li Ji as junior deputy director of the Secretariat, but Murong Wei, still smarting at an old remark, refused.

sentences.zh: 恪屢請，乃謂恪曰：「萬機之事委之叔父，伯陽一人，暐請獨裁。

translations.literal: Ke repeatedly requested; thereupon he said to Ke, "The myriad engines' affairs I entrust to uncle; for Boyang alone, Wei requests sole adjudication."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke pressed again; Murong Wei told him, "Uncle may run the whole administration; on Li Ji alone I claim the final say."

sentences.zh: 」績遂憂死。

translations.literal: Ji thereupon worried to death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji died of a broken heart.
